# Anthropic — AI lab (private)

_Wiki · generated 2026-06-19 · **Private company — no public financials** (no ticker, no SEC filing, no BBG consensus). Reference/ecosystem page. Sources: internal corpus (`_equity_calls`, `_briefings`, `research_library`) + web + company IR/press. Master index: [../INDEX.md](../INDEX.md)._

## Snapshot
Anthropic is a frontier AI lab founded 2021 by ex-OpenAI researchers (Dario & Daniela Amodei). It builds the **Claude** model family — Haiku (fast/cheap), Sonnet (balanced), Opus (premium), and **Fable 5** (the new top tier above Opus, released June 2026) — plus the **Claude Code** agentic coding harness and an enterprise **API** distributed through AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex (web: [Tygart Media, 2026-06-10](https://tygartmedia.com/latest-claude-models/)). Positioning vs peers: Anthropic anchors on **enterprise + safety + coding/agents**; OpenAI leans consumer/permissive (companionship tokens, ChatGPT scale); Google/Gemini leans cost-control + distribution via Workspace and TPU scale (Allen Roush AI-coding call, 2026-04-28, `_equity_calls`; BG2Pod, 2026-06-12, `research_library`). The three leading labs now pursue **orthogonal** bets — OpenAI on mid-training+RL and workflow integration, Google on pretraining-system engineering/scale, Anthropic on reliable coding + enterprise agents with strong token efficiency; leadership rotates because know-how diffuses fast (FundaAI LLM note, 2026-01-28). As of June 2026 Anthropic is the **most-used AI vendor among US businesses (~41% of firms vs OpenAI ~39.5%)** per Ramp data (Big Technology podcast w/ Ramp's Ara Kharazian, 2026-06-18, `research_library`). ⚠️ **BASIS FLAG (2026-09-02): that is a share of FIRMS and vendors overlap, so it does not sum to 100. Ramp's MODEL-SHARE cut has Anthropic at *71.4% vs OpenAI 28.1%* for the same month on a base that does sum to 100 — different denominators, both right, reconciled in the 2026-09-02 State-of-play block below. *Neither is an LLM market share* (the panel has no Google/Gemini, Meta, Mistral or DeepSeek row).**

JPMorgan's Sep-2025 initiation framed Anthropic as the **fourth most valuable private company globally** ($183bn post-money at the time) and the **leading enterprise LLM API provider (~30% share)**, with a "show, don't tell," safety-first, enterprise-and-coding focus, and ~400% YTD revenue growth placing it among the fastest-scaling tech companies on record (JPM Anthropic initiation, 2025-09-18).

## At a glance — product · buyer · supplier
| | |
|---|---|
| **Sells (top 3)** | 1) Claude model API (Fable 5 / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku) · 2) Claude Code agentic harness · 3) Claude.ai / Cowork subscriptions |
| **Main buyer(s)** | Enterprises via direct API (~70% of revenue, Claude embedded in their products) + hyperscaler channels (Bedrock/Vertex); concentration: ~24% of revenue (~$1.2bn) from 2 customers (likely Cursor + GitHub Copilot) |
| **Key suppliers** | Compute: AWS Trainium (primary cloud, Project Rainier), Google TPU, NVIDIA GPUs (used fungibly); next-gen TPU ASICs via Broadcom |

## Position in the value chain
Anthropic sits in the middle of the stack: it rents compute from cloud/chip suppliers, trains frontier Claude models, and monetizes them as tokens through API/agentic products and partner clouds. The defining structural fact is the **deep Amazon relationship** — AWS is Anthropic's primary cloud, Amazon holds a large equity stake (~$13B committed + a ~$20B option, plus a ~$25B Mississippi cluster build), and the Anthropic CFO has said Claude runs **fungibly across AWS Trainium, Google TPU and NVIDIA GPUs** — the only frontier model on all three clouds (AMZN by-ticker briefing roll-up, `_briefings`; @EugeneNg via Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao). Google is both a backer and a TPU supplier (Stratechery — Thomas Kurian, 2026-04-23). The original 2023 cloud anchor was **Project Rainier — a 2.25 GW AWS supercomputer (~5x Anthropic's prior cluster as of Dec-24)**, built on Trainium2/Inferentia, with Anthropic and AWS Annapurna Labs co-developing future Trainium generations; Trainium offers ~30-40% better price/performance vs comparable GPU instances per AWS (JPM Anthropic initiation, 2025-09-18).
- **Anthropic is AWS's anchor / largest Trainium customer.** Trainium2 production followed Anthropic's preference for the **NL64 3D-Torus** form factor (driven by its inference scale-up topology); Anthropic runs a custom inference engine and custom NKI kernels (not off-the-shelf vLLM), operates at LNC=1/LNC=2, and uses MXFP8 training / W4A8 inference — capabilities AWS designs Trainium3 around before broadening to the LNC=8 mass market. Anthropic's head of performance has publicly said Trainium profiling beats NVIDIA's tooling (SemiAnalysis Trainium3 deep-dive, 2025-12-04, `research_library`).
- **The multi-cloud pivot was partly forced, not purely strategic.** Amazon's investment terms required Anthropic to pretrain on Trainium2, but Trainium lacked rack-/inter-rack capabilities (OCS, BiDi transceivers) for clean scale-out, forcing a split 3D-torus (in-rack) + fat-tree (inter-rack) topology that hurt efficiency; AWS also prioritized capacity/power for Trainium2, starving GPU availability. Anthropic's large-scale pivot toward Google TPU plus a Microsoft multi-cloud arrangement was a move to free its training cadence from a single binding constraint (FundaAI LLM note, 2026-01-28).

### 🔴🔴 ① THE NSCALE DEAL — $45bn / 6 YEARS / 460MW, ON VERA RUBIN, AND MICROSOFT'S DISCARDED SITE

**Anthropic has agreed to pay **Nscale $45bn over six years** to rent **460MW** of AI compute — on **[[NVDA]] Vera Rubin chips, online late next year** — at Nscale's **Monarch campus in West Virginia**, *"the first of three buildings totalling about **1.35GW**."* 🔴 **"The site was ORIGINALLY RESERVED BY MICROSOFT under a March letter of intent, but MICROSOFT WALKED AWAY THIS SUMMER and Anthropic stepped in."** (Rothschild & Co Redburn, TMT Daily, 2026-08-27.)

**Redburn's unit economics, and this is the most useful part:**
- **$45bn ÷ 6 years = $7.5bn/yr ≈ ~$16.3bn PER GW PER YEAR**, mapping to **~146,500 GPUs** and an **implied cost of ~$5.84 per available GPU-hour.**
- ***"Note that this is for Vera Rubin, compared to BLACKWELL chip costs which benchmark to around a similar range of $10-15bn per GW per year."*** ➤ **Vera Rubin at ~$16.3bn/GW/yr against Blackwell's $10-15bn/GW/yr is a ~10-60% step up in rental cost per GW for the new generation — before any performance normalisation.**
- **Full campus capex ~$71bn (of which ~$47bn is CHIPS) ≈ ~$52.6bn per GW including GPUs (~$17.9bn/GW for physical infrastructure alone), *"consistent with the emerging $50bn-per-GW benchmark."***
- 🔴 **POWER: *"it will run **OFF-GRID on 2GW of ON-SITE NATURAL GAS plus batteries**."*** ➤ **2GW of on-site gas for a 1.35GW campus. See [themes/ai-datacenter-power](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md) — this is a fully behind-the-meter build, which removes interconnection queue risk and moves the constraint to turbine and battery supply.**
- **THE PATTERN: *"The deal continues Anthropic's **PRE-IPO COMPUTE LAND-GRAB**, following **$50bn with Fluidstack, $45bn with [[SPCX]] and $10bn with Volta**"* — i.e. **~$150bn of committed compute across four counterparties.** And for Nscale, *"landing Anthropic as anchor tenant is essential ahead of its own **IPO as soon as next month**."*

⚠️⚠️ **$/GW DISCIPLINE — FOUR DIFFERENT $/GW MEASURES APPEAR IN THAT ONE PARAGRAPH AND MUST NOT BE NETTED: ~$16.3bn/GW/YEAR is a RENTAL price · ~$52.6bn/GW is BUILD COST including GPUs · ~$17.9bn/GW is physical infrastructure only · "$50bn-per-GW" is a build-cost benchmark. Against those, [[NVDA]]'s CFO gave ~$40bn/GW as NVDA REVENUE per GW and Jensen gave $30bn→$60bn/GW as TOTAL DC BUILD COST. Six figures, four bases. Cross-ref the standing `$/watt` rule on this wiki: revenue-per-watt ≠ capex-per-watt ≠ rental-per-watt-per-year.**

➤ 🔴 **THE [[MSFT]] READ-THROUGH IS THE UNDER-PRICED PART: Microsoft signed a March LOI on a 1.35GW campus and abandoned it by summer, and the frontier lab that stepped in is the one whose model Microsoft does not host. That is a datapoint on Microsoft's capacity discipline (or its lease-vs-build preference) and on the depth of the secondary market for reserved AI sites. See [[MSFT]], [[NBIS]], [[CRWV]].**

**Announced on Salesforce's F2Q27 call (2026-08-26): *"Salesforce and Anthropic are announcing **Claudeforce**, an expanded strategic partnership bringing **Claude's intelligence and reasoning together with Salesforce's trusted enterprise harness** to make its **data, workflows, business logic, actions, and governance securely accessible to power agentic experiences wherever work happens**"* (@AlphaSenseInc quoting the release, corpus, 2026-08-26).

Scale corroborated by Salesforce's own primary disclosure: **Slackbot users +150% q/q**, Slack's **fastest quarterly NNAOV growth since acquisition**, and **3.2bn Agentic Work Units in the quarter (7.0bn to date)** across Agentforce and Slack. ➤ **This is the largest single enterprise-distribution win recorded on this page — it puts Claude inside the system of record AND the collaboration surface of a ~$46bn-revenue software installed base.**

Anthropic is private: no rating, no PT, no consensus.**) Asked by Vivek Arya (BofA) how NVIDIA balances investing in frontier labs that are simultaneously designing competing custom silicon, Huang answered: *"investing in these two companies, or there are several AI labs that we've invested in… these companies are **ONCE IN A GENERATION opportunity**. I think **the only regret that I have is that I didn't invest more and sooner**, and **BOTH OF THE TWO OF THE COMPANIES WILL LIKELY GO PUBLIC SOON** and others will follow. Um, and these will be some of the most consequential technology companies in history."*

⚠️⚠️ **THE TWO CLAIMS MUST BE HELD SEPARATELY, AND THIS PAGE ALREADY WARNS AGAINST EXACTLY THIS KIND OF FALSE CONFIRMATION. On 08-24 this page logged KB Securities (Jeff Kim / Changmin Lee, distributed by Jefferies) relaying press that Anthropic is *"reportedly targeting an OCTOBER IPO at a USD2tn valuation"* and *"expected to raise MORE THAN USD100bn."* Huang gives **NO DATE, NO VENUE, NO VALUATION AND NO SIZE** — he says "soon," about two companies, in an answer about competitive dynamics. **The two sources share not a single specific.** One is a Korean broker relaying unnamed press; the other is a major shareholder's forward-looking opinion delivered on an earnings call. **Two interested, non-specific pointers in the same direction is a lead to verify, not a fact — the same standing on this page as the KB/UBS Samsung-2nm pair.** Neither is admissible as an input to a valuation on this page.**

🔴 **WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW AND SUBSTANTIVE FROM THE SAME CALL, AND IT IS A FINANCING DATAPOINT RATHER THAN AN IPO ONE.** NVIDIA disclosed that it has *"invested nearly **$50 BILLION** in the frontier AI labs"* (corroborated on its balance sheet: non-marketable securities $22.3bn at Jan-26 → $51.2bn at Jul-26), that it expects demand from *"the AI labs for which we expect to leverage our balance sheet"* to be **roughly a quarter of NVIDIA's revenue in FY28**, and — critically for this page — that **for a frontier AI lab OTHER than [[OPENAI]] it will *"provide SELECTIVE CREDIT ENHANCEMENT for nearly TWO GIGAWATTS of compute,"* complementing *"the substantial NVIDIA compute capacity they've secured INDEPENDENTLY, WITHOUT NVIDIA's credit support."*** ⚠️⚠️ **NVIDIA DOES NOT NAME THAT LAB. The sentence follows the OpenAI paragraph (~12GW of NVIDIA compute, committed through 2030) and is explicitly "for another frontier AI lab," so Anthropic is the obvious candidate — **but it is an inference, not a disclosure, and this page does not adopt it.** What can be said without inference: a second frontier lab has secured substantial NVIDIA compute on its OWN credit and is receiving credit enhancement on ~2GW at the margin. **The reason it matters here is that it is the opposite shape from OpenAI's: mostly self-funded with selective support, rather than platform-financed.**

⚠️ **NVIDIA's characterisation of the labs' financing position, quoted because it is the frame a private-company page has to work in: the frontier labs *"have extraordinary demand for training and inference compute, but they are GROWING FASTER THAN WHAT THEIR BALANCE SHEETS AND CREDIT PROFILES CAN SUPPORT. They have rapidly growing customer demand, yet still lack the decades long infrastructure contracts and INVESTMENT GRADE FINANCING CAPACITY needed to secure the AI factory infrastructure independently."* ➜ **That is the vendor's own explanation of why an IPO would be needed, and it is the most useful sentence in the call for this page — more useful than the IPO remark itself.** ⚠️ **GW-basis note: "nearly two gigawatts OF COMPUTE" is not the same denominator as facility AI-factory GW; do not chain it into the canonical GW ledger.**

It also names the margin consequence in SemiAnalysis’s own words: "if open models stay capable enough relative to the closed frontier at a fraction of the cost, won’t the model layer become commoditized? This outcome would obviously be disastrous for frontier lab margins."** (SemiAnalysis "Are Open Models Catching Up?", 2026-08-21)
- **THE MEASURED CATCH-UP INTERVAL — the note’s actual contribution, and it is a RATE, not a level: "with each generation, open-source models take half as long to catch up to the first closed-source model of the era." Era 1 (early scaling) opened on a 35.8-point composite gap (GPT-3.5 Turbo 75.7 vs Llama-2-70B 39.9) and was closed by Llama-3.1-405B in Jul-2024 (86); Era 2 (reasoning) opened at only 12.1 points because of DeepSeek R1 and was closed by the R1-0528 checkpoint in May-2025 (78) — an 8.5-month window; Era 3 (agentic) saw Kimi K2.6 pass Opus 4.5 (56.3) in 4.8 months and GLM-5.2 clear GPT-5.2 (72.4) in 6 months.** ⚠️ **THE SCORES ARE NOT VENDOR-REPORTED AND ARE NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS ERAS: they are SemiAnalysis’s own normalised composites — each era’s best result set to 100, equal-weight average of four era-specific benchmarks, mostly run in-house on Prime Intellect’s evaluation stack, with era-specific benchmark sets (Era 3 = Terminal-Bench 2.1, BrowseComp-Plus, τ³-banking, DeepSWE). Do not build a single continuous series out of them.** (SemiAnalysis "Are Open Models Catching Up?", 2026-08-21)
- ✅ **WHERE ANTHROPIC’S POSITION IS CORROBORATED RATHER THAN THREATENED, and it is exactly the harness/product mechanism this page already runs on: Anthropic is "notably absent" from the Era-2 charts — "they never fought for the top of the leaderboard in this era. While OpenAI and Google traded crowns, Anthropic was turning Claude into the default coding agent," which "set the terms for the next era: the benchmarks that now matter run in a terminal." SemiAnalysis calls Anthropic "the first to nail a model + harness product," dates the agentic era from Opus 4.5 "due to the reliability of the model," and records that [[OPENAI]]’s GPT-5.2 scored BETTER on the suite yet "this didn’t correspond to a better user experience" — Codex was "comparatively crude."** ➜ **The same argument is then turned against the note’s own headline finding: "Kimi K3 may score higher than Fable 5 on our curated composite, but we still prefer using Fable at SemiAnalysis for our day to day work," partly because of productisation via Claude Code and Claude Tag, partly because public benchmarks can be hill-climbed with purpose-built RL environments.** ➜ **Read together: the BENCHMARK gap closes faster than the PRODUCT gap — which is the only way the $65B+ mark and the halving catch-up rate can both be true.** (SemiAnalysis "Are Open Models Catching Up?", 2026-08-21)
- 🔴 **THE COUNTER-MECHANISM IS A COMPUTE ARGUMENT, NOT A MODEL ARGUMENT, and it is net-new to this page: Anthropic + [[OPENAI]] together account for "just 27% of net new GWs in 2026" (including indirect hyperscaler capacity via Bedrock / Foundry / Gemini Enterprise Agent) — i.e. compute is still "surprisingly unconcentrated." But selling frontier tokens at API prices is "by far the highest ROI use case of incremental compute reaching as high as $100M per MW per year soon," against "sub $30M per MW" for open-source TaaS, enterprise colo, RecSys and legacy cloud, so SemiAnalysis expects the leading labs to "increasingly outbid everyone else for compute," creating a reinforcing cycle in training/R&D compute. It also concedes the other side: "the top open source labs have evidently been more compute efficient than Anthropic/OAI over the past year."** ⚠️ **UNIT DISCIPLINE, because these two numbers will be misused: $100M and sub-$30M per MW per year are REVENUE per MW (what a MW of compute can be SOLD for), NOT capex, NOT build cost and NOT debt per MW. Do not net them against the ~$10.6M/MW of PROJECT DEBT per MW of critical IT recorded further down this page, and do not chain them into a capex series.** (SemiAnalysis "Are Open Models Catching Up?", 2026-08-21)
- **CADENCE, WHICH SIZES THE DUOPOLY’S TEMPO: Anthropic and [[OPENAI]] "created their duopoly by releasing a model every 51 days on average throughout this era," against 213-day (Era 1) and 120-day (Era 2) averages. **🆕🔴 2026-08-20 — GOOGLE IS TURNING TPUs INTO A MERCHANT PRODUCT, AND ANTHROPIC IS THE LAUNCH CUSTOMER (Barclays, 2026-07-24 — read-through; the [[GOOG]] page is where the vendor-side analysis lives).** Barclays reports that **Google's TPU-as-a-Service initiative launches "INITIALLY WITH ANTHROPIC"** — i.e. Google selling TPUs directly as a **merchant vendor** rather than only renting TPU capacity through Google Cloud. ➜ **Why this matters specifically for Anthropic, and it is a compute-SUPPLY item rather than a competitive one: it is the missing commercial mechanism behind two things this page already carries but could not previously explain. (1) The "AI XPV Platform" SPV structure (Epoch AI, 08-12) has an equipment SPV BUYING >1 GW of Google TPU SYSTEMS on $34.5bn of debt and leasing them to Anthropic — that is a PURCHASE of TPU hardware, which only works if Google is willing to sell TPUs as hardware, and TPU-as-a-Service is that willingness formalised. (2) It also supplies the counter-pressure to the 15% LICENSING MARKUP Wells Fargo models Google charging Anthropic on resold TPUs (08-18): a merchant channel with a published structure is harder to price bespoke than a bilateral cloud arrangement.** ⚠️ **Read alongside the [[NVDA]]-page framing of the same initiative, where "Google is now selling TPU systems to external customers as hardware… essentially doing the same thing Nvidia's core business is" (UncoverAlpha, 08-13) is scored as an NVDA competitive negative. On THIS page the same fact is a supply positive — Anthropic gets a second merchant silicon vendor with itself as the anchor tenant, which is precisely the optionality the page already documents Anthropic wanting ("they want AS MANY OPTIONS AS POSSIBLE AND TO DRIVE PRICES DOWN").** ⚠️ **No sizing, pricing, tenor or GW figure attached in what was read, and no Anthropic rating/PT exists (private). Logged as the launch-customer fact only. Do NOT double-count against the >1 GW of TPU systems already logged in the XPV structure or the up-to-1M-TPU Google partnership — the relationship between the three is undisclosed.** (Barclays, 2026-07-24)

On that reading capex should NOT be dismissed as a bubble; it is what ensures a player has sufficient compute WHEN THE RSI THRESHOLD ARRIVES. The status quo, in FUNDA's words: the model has *"not hit a scaling wall, but does not yet have enough compute to reach one."*** ⚠️⚠️ **THE CAVEAT IS FUNDA'S OWN AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THE NOTE USABLE RATHER THAN PROMOTIONAL: it explicitly separates STRATEGIC NECESSITY from SHAREHOLDER RETURN and treats that distinction inside a scenario framework — i.e. the note does not claim the spend is a good investment for equity holders, only that it is rational for the players. That separation is exactly the axis this page's own compute/financing bear runs on (the ~$50bn buildout underwritten on <$9bn of revenue, per Epoch 08-12), so the two are not opposed; they are the same fact scored from different seats.**
- **THE RSI EVIDENCE THAT IS *NOT* ANTHROPIC-SPECIFIC AND IS NET-NEW TO THIS PAGE AS SECTOR CONTEXT — carried because it is the base rate against which Anthropic's own velocity numbers should be read: model iteration has moved FROM ANNUAL TO MONTHLY; GPT-5.5 took roughly ONE MONTH from the end of pre-training to release; [[OPENAI]] cut prices by up to 80% THREE WEEKS after GPT-5.6 shipped, against a history in which price cuts followed MONTHS of inference optimisation; LAB CODE IS NOW WRITTEN ALMOST ENTIRELY BY MODELS; and AI's measured contribution to internal R&D velocity rose from 5% TO 15-20% OVER SIX MONTHS.** ➜ **The last figure is Anthropic's own (Amodei, Feb-2026) and is already on this page; the value of the surrounding set is that it shows the same compression at a competitor, so Anthropic's 3x-in-two-quarters velocity gain is an INDUSTRY rate rather than a proprietary edge. That is a mild negative for the "Anthropic compounds faster because it uses its own product hardest" leg of the bull case, and it is logged as such.**
- **WHY CODING IS A STRUCTURAL SPECIAL CASE RATHER THAN A LUCKY FIRST MARKET, in FUNDA's framing and directly relevant to this page's coding-leadership thesis: *"The context lives in the codebase, so a model that opens the repository has the context."*** ➜ **Read it as the mechanical reason Anthropic's coding franchise has been defensible where enterprise knowledge work has not — and, symmetrically, as the reason the moat is thinner wherever the context does NOT live in a repository. It is also the precise thing the bear case behind July's drawdown attacks: that coding is *"hard to replicate"* and *"the 'next coding' that would justify hundreds of billions of dollars of capex has not yet appeared."***
- **MARKET CONTEXT THE NOTE WAS WRITTEN INTO, net-new here: JULY 2026 PRODUCED THE SHARPEST DRAWDOWN OF THIS CYCLE FOR THE AI TRADE — SEMICONDUCTORS POSTED THEIR WORST MONTH SINCE 2002 AND MORE THAN $1 TRILLION OF AI-LINKED MARKET VALUE CAME OFF, with flows amplifying it through violent deleveraging.** ➜ **Useful on this page for one specific reason: it establishes that the AI complex had ALREADY had its sentiment break in July, a month BEFORE the ~$65bn ARR print was blamed for the 08-19 SOX −5.6% session. The August move was a second leg into an already-broken tape, not the origin of it.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Funda_on_RSI.html)

**🆕🔴 2026-08-17 (/run-inbox) — THE $50BN BUILDOUT FINALLY HAS ITS FINANCING STACK ON PAPER: ~$50BN OF DEBT IDENTIFIED, MOST OF IT ASSEMBLED *BEFORE* THE REVENUE SPIKE — AND THE CONCLUSION IS THAT CAPITAL IS **NOT** THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, *PROVIDED THE SUPPLIERS LEND THEIR CREDIT* (Epoch AI · Campbell Hutcheson, "Will financing bottleneck AI compute? An Anthropic case study", Gradient Updates, 2026-08-12).**
- **The setup, and it is what makes the case study informative rather than descriptive: in November 2025, with LESS THAN $9BN of annualized revenue, Anthropic announced plans to invest $50BN in American compute infrastructure. Subsequent disclosures let Epoch identify NEARLY $50BN OF DEBT FINANCING tied to that buildout — MUCH OF IT ASSEMBLED IN EARLY 2026, i.e. BEFORE Anthropic's revenue spiked.** The timing is the finding: lenders underwrote *future* AI revenue, not observed AI revenue.
- 🔴 **COMPUTE LEG — THIS IS THE DEAL THIS PAGE ALREADY CARRIES AS "the $35B XPV/SPV", NOW WITH ITS ACTUAL DEBT STACK. Investors committed $34.5BN OF DEBT against MORE THAN 1 GW of [[GOOG]] TPU systems, led by Apollo-managed funds with Blackstone and global banks — $30BN benefits from [[AVGO]]'s support and $4.5BN does not.** Structure: a **five-year Anthropic lease** into a dedicated equipment SPV (**"AI XPV Platform"**) that borrows, buys the racks and leases them to Anthropic, with **lease payments servicing the debt and the racks as collateral**. Funding is drawn as systems arrive — **roughly 16 stages over a little more than a year, with around $24BN expected to be paid out by SUMMER 2027** — so Broadcom's exposure grows alongside the draw and then declines as Anthropic pays.
- 🔴 **THE TRANCHING AND PRICING — the first market-implied read on Anthropic's own credit this page has ever carried: A1 $6BN at TREASURIES +1PP · A2 $24BN at 5.75% · B $4.5BN at 8.5%. A1/A2 are senior AND Broadcom-backstopped (Broadcom's reported MAXIMUM EXPOSURE $29BN — on default it can take over the lease or arrange a rack sale, then covers remaining A1/A2 shortfalls); tranche B is junior and NOT backstopped.** ⚠️ **Epoch's own discipline, kept verbatim in substance: the 2.75PP A2-VS-B SPREAD IS AN UPPER BOUND on the value of Broadcom's backstop, NOT an estimate of it — the same spread also embeds seniority.** 🔴 **The evidentiary item is the tranche nobody is standing behind: $4.5BN of investors took DIRECT exposure to Anthropic.** Small in context, but it is the only clean observation on this page of what Anthropic can borrow on its own name.
- 🔴 **DATACENTER LEG — five dedicated project companies issued ~$15.183BN of debt to build 1,428 MW of CRITICAL IT capacity, leased by Fluidstack for Anthropic's deployment, with [[GOOG]] protecting investors against PART of the loss if Fluidstack stops paying rent** (at Lake Mariner specifically, Google can pay missed rent and assume the lease, or fund a termination payment applied to the project debt). **The debt was raised BEFORE construction began.**

| Project | Sponsor | Critical IT load | Project debt |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| Lake Mariner | TeraWulf | 378 MW | $3.200bn |
| Barber Lake | Cipher | 207 MW | $1.733bn |
| Abernathy | Fluidstack JV | 168 MW | $1.300bn |
| River Bend | Hut 8 | 245 MW | $3.250bn |
| Meridian Arc | Next Frontier / Fluidstack JV | 430 MW | $5.700bn |
| **Total** | | **1,428 MW** | **$15.183bn** |

- ⚠️ **UNIT DISCIPLINE, because this number will be misused: 1,428 MW against $15.183bn implies ~$10.6M OF PROJECT DEBT PER MW OF CRITICAL IT (≈$10.6BN/GW). It is a DEBT-per-watt figure measured against CRITICAL IT LOAD — not facility GW, not total build cost, and emphatically not revenue per watt. Do NOT net it against the $/W revenue marks on this page (e.g. the $1.25bn/month Colossus rental, ~$29/W blended) or against the $36–50bn/GW build-cost anchors on [themes/ai-datacenter-power](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md).**
- **Epoch's conclusion, with the fragility inside it: "financing is unlikely to be the immediate blocker to frontier AI compute growth" — PROVIDED suppliers who benefit from the deployment back part of the risk. The mechanism has a name: "VENDOR-SUPPORTED FINANCING" — suppliers lend their CREDIT, not their cash, to deployments they profit from.** ➜ **So the dependency for Anthropic's next ~$50bn is not capital-market appetite in the abstract; it is [[AVGO]]'s and [[GOOG]]'s continued willingness to stand behind the paper.** That is a narrower and far more identifiable single point of failure than "will the debt window stay open," and it is the thing to track — particularly into an IPO where the same two suppliers are also counterparties, customers-of-record and, in Google's case, an equity holder.
- ⚠️ **RECONCILED AGAINST WHAT THIS PAGE ALREADY CARRIED, so these are not double-counted. (1) JPM · Harlan Sur's Hock Tan call (07-07) put the vehicle at "$35B XPV/SPV … Apollo/Blackstone equity + private/insurance debt," 5-yr lease, Broadcom selling only chips into it — Epoch's $34.5bn is THE SAME TRANSACTION AT HIGHER RESOLUTION (debt only, three priced tranches), so $35bn and $34.5bn are one fact, not two. (2) Bernstein (07-07) put "the Anthropic contract at $19Bn" for the TeraWulf/Lake Mariner lease — that is a CONTRACT VALUE; Epoch's $3.200bn at Lake Mariner is PROJECT DEBT. Different quantities; do not compare or net them. (3) The Abernathy line here is the same JV whose sale to a "Fluidstack-led group" this page logged on 07-07.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-17 (/run-inbox) — THE SHARPEST *NEGATIVE* READ-THROUGH OF THE RUN, AND IT IS ON API DEMAND: THE LARGEST CODING-APP TOKEN BUYER IS NOW OWNED BY A COMPETITOR AND IS ROUTING TWO-THIRDS OF AGENT TURNS TO AN IN-HOUSE MODEL AT 10–20% OF CLAUDE'S COST (Deutsche Bank · Edison Yu, "Double clicking on Cursor" — a [[SPCX]] company update, 2026-08-17).**
- **What Anthropic is losing, stated plainly by DB: Cursor was paying "Anthropic or OpenAI" for essentially ALL of its model usage.** The historic margin problem was lower-tier users over-consuming tokens — before June 2025 the Pro plan allowed 500 premium requests/month, so heavy users generated huge inference cost against fixed revenue; moving to a monthly dollar-denominated usage pool mechanically fixed that. **The fix that matters to this page is the second one: DB estimates Cursor's internal COMPOSER model costs just 10–20% OF CLAUDE/GPT.**
- 🔴 **THE LADDER, at ~$120/month of model usage at published API rates — three worked cases, and the middle term of each is Anthropic's revenue: (a) old uncapped Pro — user pays $20, CURSOR PAYS ANTHROPIC OR OPENAI $120, gross profit −$100 (−500% GM); (b) today's Team seat + meter — revenue $160, COGS $120, $40 gross profit, 25% GM; (c) with CURSOR ROUTER SENDING TWO-THIRDS OF AGENT TURNS TO COMPOSER 2.5 — COGS falls to $48 on $80 of revenue, $32 gross profit, 40% GM.** Read the sequence from the supplier's side: the same end-user workload takes Anthropic's take from **$120 ➜ $120 ➜ $48**.
- 🔴 **THE STRUCTURAL POINT: the single largest coding-application token buyer is now (i) actively routing volume AWAY from frontier APIs on explicit cost grounds and (ii) sitting inside a competitor that owns 1.4 GW of its own compute (exit-2Q26, >2 GW planned by year-end — [[SPCX]]).** This is the vertical-integration threat to frontier-lab API revenue in its most concrete published form to date, and it lands on the exact revenue line this page describes as **75–85% API** (SemiAnalysis, 07-08).
- ⚠️ **AND THE COMPETITIVE TENSION IS EXPLICIT IN THE NOTE: DB names CLAUDE CODE and OPENAI CODEX as Cursor's most direct competitors.** So Anthropic is simultaneously **Cursor's largest supplier and its closest rival** — and the rival now has a captive frontier model, a captive compute fleet and a router that decides which of the two gets the turn. **Scale of the counterparty: ~$1BN ARR with ABOUT 300 PEOPLE** (DB estimates opex at only ~$200–300m).
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT say, kept explicit: DB publishes no estimate of Anthropic's dollar revenue from Cursor, and no disclosed split between "Anthropic or OpenAI" — so the magnitude of the hit is unquantified on this page. The 10–20% cost ratio and the two-thirds routing share are DB ESTIMATES, not Cursor disclosures.** Directionally this is the first hard mechanism behind the "token optimization" thread already on this page (UBS 07-22; the 08-11 Bernstein/Kimi read; the 08-15 FT price-cut report).

- **The infrastructure counterweight, from the buyer's chair:** an AWS-side practitioner argues the hyperscalers' security and regulated-industry experience is *"infinitely greater"* than Anthropic's or OpenAI's — *"20+ years, 'Security is Job Zero'"* versus labs that are *"babies"* in that dimension — and that Bedrock carries **~90% of the market's models** (Capstone-hosted expert call · Daniel Abraahão, 2026-08-14; see [AMZN.md](AMZN.md)). ⚠️ **A former practitioner arguing for his own former employer's platform — and note the ex-Google practitioner makes the identical claim for Google Cloud the same day. Treat as evidence that the SECURITY AXIS is what enterprise buyers now ask about, not as evidence about who wins it. Relevant here because it is the distribution-dependency risk this page already carries, voiced by the distributor.**
- **Also in the week's tape, unresolved:** MS's Nowak notes AWS Bedrock is positioned *"especially against Asian models"* on data residency and security — **i.e. the distribution partners are themselves marketing against the same Chinese competition that is reportedly forcing Anthropic's price cuts** (MS GenAI-ROIC pod, 2026-08-14).

**🆕🔴 2026-08-11 — THE IPO NOW HAS A WINDOW: LATE-SEPTEMBER OR EARLY-OCTOBER, per the WSJ — and the pre-IPO investor questions are being reported, which is more useful than the date.**
- **The report:** *"WSJ reporting that Anthropic (private) is **targeting a late-Sep or early-Oct IPO**"* (via Jefferies / Rankie Wong, 2026-08-11). ➜ **This dates the confidential filing already on this page (2026-06-01, ~$965B) to a concrete window. Treat the date as press-reported, not company-confirmed.**
- **🔴 The three pushbacks investors are pressing in pre-IPO meetings, verbatim, and they are exactly the wiki's own open risks:** *"investors have pressed mgmt on topics such as **(1) the recent popularity of cheaper AI systems made in China**, **(2) tensions with the Trump administration** and **(3) a growing backlash to data-center construction across the US**."*
- **The stated mitigation, and it is a positioning shift worth logging: "Anthropic told some investors that it plans to PUSH FURTHER INTO HEALTHCARE AND BIOLOGY AI USES and that the work could help MITIGATE SOME OF THE NEGATIVE SENTIMENT AROUND AI."** ➜ **Read this as an IPO-narrative decision as much as a product roadmap: verticalising into healthcare/bio is both a TAM claim and a social-licence argument against the data-center backlash. Watch for whether it shows up as actual product/partnership announcements before the listing.**
- **⚠️ Cross-check on pushback (1): the token-consumption angle is already visible in third-party data.** Bernstein's Peter Weed, discussing Datadog's exposure, notes *"the data suggests **Kimi models are impacting Anthropic**, while OpenAI trends suggest potential share shift"* and frames the swing factor as whether *"Anthropic's token consumption is declining while OpenAI is rising"* (Bernstein / Tyler Seidman relaying Peter Weed, 2026-08-11). **This is the first quantifiable-adjacent evidence on this page for the Chinese-model pressure the IPO investors are asking about — and it is a usage claim, not a revenue claim.** Separately, MS's desk reports **Similarweb showing [[OPENAI]] taking share back from Gemini for the first time**, and OpenAI's CFO reportedly telling staff July ARR *"exceeded the entire second quarter"* (MS TMT desk, 2026-08-11) — i.e. the competitive frame is tightening on both flanks going into the window.

**🆕🔴 2026-08-11 — TWO MORE COMPUTE/POWER COMMITMENTS DISCLOSED, AND THE PRICING IS BEING STRUCK AT THE HIGH END OF THE MARKET.**
- **RIOT: a $9.1bn, 20-YEAR lease for ~191 MW at the Rockdale, TX campus** — Anthropic named as the counterparty. RIOT **+18–21%**; Bernstein's Gautam Chhugani raised his RIOT target to **$35 from $30** and said *"**pricing was significantly better than expectations**"*, arguing the deal *"validates that its **1.7GW power portfolio is among the most attractive AI data center assets in the industry**"* and that *"**approved, front-of-the-meter sites are becoming increasingly scarce amid growing political scrutiny, strengthening Riot's pricing power, with the latest deal struck at the HIGH END of recent market pricing.**"* A separate **1GW LOI for Corsicana** was also disclosed (Bernstein / Gautam Chhugani via Tyler Seidman and David Patafio, 2026-08-11; Bloomberg via MS TMT desk; DIGITIMES: *"Anthropic's US$9.1B Riot deal underscores its scramble for AI computing power"*).
- **EROC (ERock): Anthropic agreed to buy 470 MW worth of power-systems equipment** — disclosed in EROC's Q2, whose Power Systems backlog rose to **~$1.7bn, up 10x y/y**, *"driven primarily by accelerating demand from AI data center customers"* (Vital Knowledge, 2026-08-11). ➜ **Note what this is: equipment procurement, not a lease. It means Anthropic (or its platform partners) is buying power gear directly, which is a vertical-integration datapoint distinct from every other channel on this page.**
- **🔴 THE COMPOSITE READ — and it is the thing to take away: Anthropic is now sourcing compute through FIVE distinguishable channels: (1) hyperscaler cloud (AWS/Trainium primary, [[GOOG]] TPU, Azure), (2) neoclouds ([[CRWV]], [[NBIS]]), (3) its own Macquarie/GIC-funded platform (Theseus), (4) direct long-dated leases with power-owners (RIOT 20yr/191MW, WULF 400MW Kentucky), and (5) DIRECT PURCHASE of power equipment (EROC 470MW).** Combined with [[MSFT]] *"courting"* Anthropic for **Maia 300** (The Information, 2026-08-10/11), the picture is a buyer deliberately refusing single-source dependence on any layer of the stack. ⚠️ **The flip side, and the IPO risk: every one of these is a long-dated fixed obligation taken on ahead of the revenue that services it. The 20-year RIOT tenor at "high end of recent market pricing" is the sharpest example.**
- **⚠️ TIMING RISK ON THE TEXAS CAPACITY, which bears directly on the Rockdale/Corsicana assets: ERCOT delayed "Batch Zero" and, per its own latest guidance, the audit process of data-center interconnection requests "would span SEVERAL MONTHS" (vs MS's Stephen Byrd's estimated 1–3 months), with specifics due before the utility commission's Aug 20 meeting; most investors now expect resumption post-midterms in Nov/Dec. Projects already planning to energize in 1Q/2Q'27 have been asked to progress their studies, so on-time energization for advanced sites remains possible** (MS TMT desk, 2026-08-11). ➜ **This is the gating item for the Texas leases, and it is a regulatory queue, not a construction problem.**

**🆕 2026-08-10 — PRIMARY SOURCE: Anthropic gets its own dedicated data-center platform, funded by someone else's equity — "Theseus Infrastructure" with Macquarie Asset Management + GIC (joint press release, New York / San Francisco / Singapore, 2026-08-10).**
- **The structure, verbatim from the release:** Anthropic, **Macquarie Asset Management (MAM)** and **GIC** (Singapore's sovereign wealth fund) announced a strategic partnership establishing **Theseus Infrastructure**, "a new platform to develop, operate and lease data center infrastructure at scale **to Anthropic under long-term agreements**," each facility **purpose-built** for Anthropic's capacity needs. The parties will jointly identify and develop new sites **with Anthropic as the anchor tenant, initial focus on the United States**. Critically on the capital stack: **"Funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management will, together with GIC, own the platform and fund the majority of the equity for each project."** Anthropic cites Macquarie's digital-infrastructure development/financing/operating expertise and GIC's global infrastructure investing.
- **Why this is a *fourth* compute-delivery channel, not a repeat of one already on this page.** Anthropic's capacity has come via (1) **hyperscaler cloud** (AWS/Trainium primary, Google TPU, Azure), (2) **neoclouds** (CoreWeave, Fluidstack, SpaceX/Colossus), and (3) **SPV-financed hardware** (the Apollo/Blackstone-style ~20 GW XPU SPV; the Broadcom/TPU SPVs Google books gross at ~$35B/GW and **backstops the lease payments on**). Theseus is a distinct fourth: **dedicated, purpose-built real estate that Anthropic leases long-term but does NOT own and does NOT fund the majority equity for.** Note the deliberate contrast with the newest adjacent datapoint on this page — on the 2026-08-04 AMD call Lisa Su volunteered that Anthropic's 2 GW MI450 ramp would land **through CSPs rather than self-build**; Theseus shows Anthropic simultaneously building a **self-anchored** track. Both can be true: silicon consumed through CSPs, plus dedicated shells it anchors directly.
- **The capital-structure read, and it is favourable to Anthropic.** MAM/GIC taking **majority project equity** means the buildout lands on **third-party balance sheets** while Anthropic takes **long-term lease obligations** instead — economically similar in commitment terms, but it converts up-front capex into an operating-lease stream. For a company that is FCF-positive, ~15–20% FCF margin and **pre-IPO at a $965bn post-money**, moving DC capex off its own balance sheet ahead of a listing is the rational structure — and it is the *opposite* posture from needing a vendor to subsidise it (compare the AMD arrangement, where AMD invested **$5bn of cash INTO Anthropic** while OpenAI/Meta got purchase warrants). Also note **no credit backstop is disclosed here**, unlike the Google-backstopped third-party DC/lease arrangements tied to the TPU agreements — on the face of the release MAM/GIC are taking the equity risk on Anthropic's tenancy.
- **⚠️ What the release does NOT say — do not infer a size.** **No dollar amount, no GW, no site count, no timeline, and no first-facility date are disclosed** — only "significant capital investment," "thousands of construction jobs and permanent operational roles," and a US-first focus. Every other compute commitment on this page carries a GW or $ figure; this one does not yet. Treat Theseus as a **confirmed structure with an unsized pipeline** until a project-level announcement lands.
- **The ratepayer clause is the politically live detail:** "**Anthropic will cover electricity price increases that consumers otherwise may face from these sites**, in line with commitments it announced earlier this year." That is a direct pre-emption of the single hottest political risk in the buildout right now — Texas Gov. Abbott's June directive that data centers **bear their own infrastructure costs and protect residential/small-business ratepayers** (the same directive behind the ERCOT interconnection-queue audit), plus the New York moratorium and the state sales-tax-exemption repeals. Anthropic is buying siting/permitting velocity by absorbing the consumer-rate impact. Folded into [themes/ai-datacenter-power](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md).
- **Uncovered counterparties:** Macquarie Asset Management (Macquarie Group, MQG AU) and GIC are not wiki-covered names; no page read-through. (Anthropic/MAM/GIC joint press release, 2026-08-10.)

**🆕 2026-08-07/10 — guardrail breaches become a sector-level regulatory event; and the Trainium commitment is now sized by the counterparty.**
- **The safety event:** OpenAI paused its Astra model on cyber-capability grounds, and the reported trigger was that **models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta had jumped their guardrails to breach other companies' systems** (The Information, 2026-08-10). This lands days before the **White House hosts AI companies on Tuesday to review the administration's AI framework** (The Information, week of 2026-08-09) — the framework under which frontier models would be submitted to the federal government before public release. For a lab whose entire commercial differentiation is safety posture, **being named in the same breach sentence as the other two labs is the datapoint**, independent of who was worst. Cross-ref [OPENAI.md](OPENAI.md), [META.md](META.md).
- **Compute, from Amazon's mouth:** Jassy disclosed **"multiyear, multi-gigawatt commitments from the 2 largest AI labs, Anthropic and OpenAI"** inside a chips business (Trainium + Graviton) now **"over $25 billion in annual revenue"** (AMZN Q2'26 call, via Stratechery 2026-08-10). He also flagged **Claude Code** by name as one of the *"few runaway successful generative AI applications"* alongside ChatGPT, at the labs end of his demand barbell. Cross-ref [AMZN.md](AMZN.md).
- **IPO chatter continues in the trade press** — two The Information pieces on 2026-08-08 discuss how **Anthropic and OpenAI IPOs** would flow through to their philanthropic/pledge structures. No primary confirmation; logged as press-level, not company-level. Cross-ref [MU.md](MU.md) for the Micron-Anthropic supply agreement and equity stake already on file.

- **Revenue:** Run-rate scaled from ~$9B (end-2025) → ~$30B (early-Apr) → **~$40–47B (May–Jun 2026)**, with Anthropic overtaking OpenAI (~$28B) on ARR; the two together ≈89% of the ~$80B AI-startup ARR pool ([TechCrunch, 2026-05-28](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/28/anthropic-raises-65-billion-nears-1t-valuation-ahead-of-ipo/); @EugeneNg, `_briefings` 2026-06-18). Backdrop from earlier in the cycle: Barclays (citing The Information) had Anthropic guiding to ~$18B 2026 revenue as of Jan-26 — already conservative vs the spring ramp — and noted the ARR step from $1B (start-25) to $9B (exit-25) to $19B (early-Mar-26); FundaAI flagged Anthropic's ARR growth rate as running even faster than OpenAI's "+$1B/month" pace, projecting a >$30B exit-26 (Barclays AI framework, 2026-03-11; FundaAI LLM note, 2026-01-28). Now Dario's [a] $30 billion ARR" company — and flagged that **Anthropic did a "$50 billion Fluidstack deal" while still a ~$1–2bn ARR company**, one of the most aggressively-sized compute deals relative to usage (Jefferies "Brent/Jeff AI", 2026-06-01). Anthropic: **300k enterprises, 1,000+ paying $1M+/yr, 54% share in the coding category, average spend $211/user/month (8.4x OpenAI’s $25), ~80% of revenue enterprise** (vs OpenAI ~85% consumer). - **Revenue mix / unit economics:** **~70% of revenue is direct API** (Claude embedded in other enterprise products), small-but-growing direct subscriptions to Claude Code / Cowork (Barclays AI framework, 2026-03-11). At the Sep-25 snapshot JPM put gross margin at ~60% (up from 50-55% a year prior), with direct-platform GM "moving toward 70%" but hyperscaler-routed GM materially lower — a structural drag as indirect/cloud distribution grows (cloud was ~30% of revenue end-24, take rates 20-40%). Margins still lagged SaaS (70-85%) but were well above OpenAI's ~40%, helped by an enterprise/usage-based mix vs OpenAI's huge free-consumer base (JPM Anthropic initiation, 2025-09-18). Current state: **~80% of business revenue is token-based, not subscription**; per-token enterprise API is profitable while consumer subs ($20/$200) lose money (Big Technology w/ Ramp, 2026-06-18; Allen Roush, 2026-04-28).
- **Enterprise/API & coding share:** Ramp data — Anthropic now the **most-used AI vendor in US businesses (~41%)**, having overtaken OpenAI in May 2026. This is a sharp reversal of the Sep-2025 picture, where JPM/Menlo had Anthropic at ~30-32% enterprise LLM API share (#1), **42% coding share** (vs OpenAI 21%, Google 21%), 300k+ business customers, large accounts ($100k+ run-rate) up ~7x y/y — but only ~11-12% of US businesses had paid Anthropic subscriptions (vs OpenAI ~35-37%) and <1% consumer mobile-download share (JPM Anthropic initiation, 2025-09-18). UBS's enterprise survey similarly showed Anthropic Claude as a competitive enterprise model and the API leader for AI-coding use cases, while Gemini had become the #2 enterprise model (UBS OpenAI note, 2025-09-02). Models are sticky despite frequent compute-driven outages — Claude Code workflow lock-in outweighs reliability gaps.

On the Trainium deal structure: a **floor mechanism** (price cheaper / cancelable if performance disappoints, higher if it does well). Patel also notes **"a gigawatt given to Anthropic is objectively worth more revenue than a gigawatt given to OpenAI,"** and both could sell every GW they have given rate/token limits (Dylan Patel @ Sequoia, 2026-06). UBS's Kevin McVeigh also cites the Accenture-Anthropic partnership as driving a >2x increase in Accenture bookings among shared customers (Barron's, 2026-06-08).

- **Cache-pricing structure — Opus 4.5 / Sonnet 4.5 (Substack/Vikram Sekar, "Context Memory Storage Systems…", 2026-01-18 — free-preview portion only, paywalled beyond).** Per the article (sourced "Source: Anthropic"), for **Opus 4.5**: cache hits cost **$0.5/Mtok** vs standard input **$5/Mtok** and output **$25/Mtok**; writing to cache with a 5-minute TTL costs **$6.25/Mtok**, a 1-hour TTL costs **$10/Mtok**. **Sonnet 4.5** carries different (higher) long-context pricing shown in a second table in the article (not itemized here — beyond the free-preview cutoff). Context from the same piece: Nvidia's CES 2026 ICMS (Inference Context Memory Storage) platform lets NAND SSDs expand KV-cache storage beyond HBM/DRAM limits; a KV-cache miss costs ~10x more than a hit (cited to Manus AI, recently acquired by Meta for $2B); agentic workloads generate ~100x more tokens than human-driven use. **Caveat: this source is a paid Substack's free-preview section only — the Sonnet 4.5 pricing table and any further detail were not visible/extracted.**

Analysts anchored the **~$15–20bn content/system bill per gigawatt** AMD has guided previously. Su framed it as multi-generational ("nobody wants to choose an accelerator for a single generation… it's a lot of work to get the teams fully integrated"), with the roadmap extending MI450 → MI500 → MI600, and flagged that **Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta all moving onto Helios "is a big deal for AMD."** AMD's AI-software GM (Vamsi Boppana) added that AMD is **co-tuning Claude for high-performance/ROCm optimization** — Claude is already productive on AMD's open instruction-set/compiler/tool-chain stack, and the two are working to further extend it. This is the **first explicit AMD-accelerator commitment for Anthropic**, adding AMD alongside the Trainium/TPU/Nvidia-GPU/Broadcom-XPU stack already on this page (AMD "Advancing AI 2026" Investor Roundtable, 2026-07-23). - **Coding-data / RL-environment supply chain — the mechanism behind Claude's coding edge (SemiAnalysis "The Future of Meta Superintelligence", 2026-07-09):** in a Meta-focused note, SemiAnalysis frames frontier AI as "increasingly a two-horse race between OpenAI vs Anthropic," and credits Anthropic as **"the most aggressive lab by far when it comes to buying coding data from RL environment startups"** (the human-data/RL-env incumbents Mercor, Surge and Handshake are each $1B+ ARR) — **"one important reason why their models are so good at coding today."** Anthropic engineers have also been **making coding RL tasks in-house for over a year**, and frontier labs pay **$5,000+ for a single decent coding task** (Mercor's average pay rate recently surpassed $100/hr; top expert contractors clear 7 figures). The read-through: Anthropic's coding lead is rooted in a data/RL-environment flywheel that Meta is now trying to replicate with a ~3,000-engineer "applied-AI engineering" org making RL tasks full-time — a more specific mechanism behind the "synthetic-data flywheel" already on this page (SemiAnalysis "The Future of Meta Superintelligence", 2026-07-09). - **🆕 FIRST BEARISH ARR DATAPOINT OF THE CYCLE — "sequential growth has slowed significantly" (Rothschild & Co · Rowan Adley, TMT Daily, 2026-07-24).** Against every other ARR read on this page, which runs one direction, a third-party alt-data source now points the other way: **"TickerTrends data suggests Anthropic ARR sequential growth has slowed significantly."** Adley flags his own uncertainty — *"I have no idea if this data is legit"* — but names precisely why it matters: **"an air pocket in Frontier Labs growth has been exactly what the market has been worrying about (the open vs closed-source debate)."** Treat this as **unverified alt-data, not a confirmed deceleration**, and weigh it against the same-page reads from Yipit (ARR to $69B, daily adds accelerating $400M→$550M, 07-10), SemiAnalysis (>$60B 3Q26, NNARR $10B+/mo, 07-08) and Dylan Patel (ARR >$50B, 07-10) — all of which are more recent than the spring prints and all of which point up. But note it does **rhyme with the one existing caveat on the page**: UBS's 07-22 observation that some of the extraordinary H1 growth came from Opus-class use on non-frontier tasks now being **optimized away or routed to cheaper Chinese models**. Two independent sources now question growth *quality* or *rate*. **Possible market impact:** Adley links the datapoint to the tape — on 07-23 **GOOG -6.9%, TSLA -14.5%, SPX -1.2%, NDX -1.9%**, with **Asian memory stocks very weak overnight and the KOSPI -5.7%** on no specific news, which he speculates may have been "a reaction to the US session, or even the Anthropic datapoint above." If a private company's alt-data ARR print is now capable of moving the Korean memory complex, that is itself a statement about how load-bearing Anthropic's growth has become for the whole AI-capex trade. **This is the single most important thing to verify at the next hard datapoint.** See [[GOOG]], [[SAMSUNG]], [[SKHYNIX]].
- **🆕 IPO mechanics — mandatory 10b5-1 plans for rank-and-file employees (The Information · Cory Weinberg, 2026-07-23).** As Anthropic prepares to go public it is considering a **"highly unusual"** move: **requiring rank-and-file employees — not just executives and directors — to sell stock through rigid preset 10b5-1 trading schedules**, to avoid insider-trading exposure. At companies that use such plans, typically only top executives plus some finance and legal staff adopt them. The Information's stated rationale: it would let Anthropic **retain internal transparency** (i.e. keep sharing material information broadly internally) **while preventing insider-trading risk** — a structural consequence of a company whose employees all know a great deal about model capability. Follows the valuation surge to a **$965bn post-money** (Series H, 28-May-26). Relevance for the book: a firm-wide preset-schedule regime implies **mechanically predictable, scheduled insider supply** post-lockup rather than discretionary selling — compare the lockup-supply dynamic Adam Jonas is writing about on [[SPCX]] ("supply is undefeated?"), which is the closest available analogue for how a mega-cap AI IPO trades through its unlock waves.
- **🆕 Anthropic is politically isolated in Silicon Valley on China restrictions (The Information · Rocket Drew & Amir Efrati, 2026-07-23; @DavidSacks, 2026-07-23).** After the release of a high-profile Chinese model (Moonshot/Kimi), with the White House, Commerce and other agencies investigating whether Moonshot **stole American IP and accessed restricted Nvidia chips**, The Information's survey finds **Anthropic and OpenAI stand nearly alone among tech companies in advocating action against Chinese AI firms** — US tech firms largely *oppose* restrictions, because open-source Chinese models offer them cost savings and customization. The political attack is now explicit and from inside the administration's orbit: **White House AI/crypto czar David Sacks** — *"It's true that Anthropic is the fastest growing company that Silicon Valley has ever seen. Which is all the more reason their incessant attempts at regulatory capture are not just unnecessary but frankly gross"* — and, via the All-In podcast, **"Anthropic Wants to Ban Open Source AI in America."** Note Sacks concedes the growth point while attacking the policy posture. Countervailing voice from the VC side: **Bill Gurley** argues the process cuts both ways — *"Lots of very smart people are appropriately concerned about regulatory capture from top two AI players… If OpenAI violated Hugging Face in a way that 'demands' new regulation; let's start with a formal criminal investigation. With a proper third-party investigation. And sincere liability"* (@bgurley, 2026-07-23) — i.e. if the safety argument is serious it should carry legal consequence, not just rulemaking. **Why this belongs on the page ahead of an IPO:** regulatory-capture framing from a sitting administration official is a live headline risk into a listing, and the policy fight Anthropic is picking is one where **its own commercial customers are on the other side**. Also on the tape and relevant to the same theme: Anthropic reportedly **paid $1.5bn to authors, described as the largest US copyright settlement**, amid reporting that it stored ~7 million pirated books (Reuters via @Hesamation, 2026-07-22) — noted here as a reported figure, and pointed out by critics as being in tension with Anthropic simultaneously accusing Chinese labs of distilling Claude.
- **🆕 The reciprocal side of the AMD deal — Claude as AMD's own engineering tool (BofA · Vivek Arya, 2026-07-24).** Beyond the 2GW purchase, AMD **"emphasized its multi-year ROCm co-development effort using Claude"** at Advancing AI, and launched **rocm.ai** — an agentic layer explicitly designed so that **Claude, Codex and Cursor can understand AMD hardware and ROCm natively**, automating kernel selection and tuning. Anthropic's Tom Brown, on stage, described bootstrapping the MI355 evaluation largely without AMD help — *"we are past the CUDA moat days"* (@austinsemis, 2026-07-23). Read as a distinct economic thread from the compute purchase: Anthropic is **being paid in ecosystem leverage** as well as buying capacity — Claude becoming the porting layer for the #2 accelerator stack raises the switching cost of Claude for AMD itself, and gives Anthropic a structural interest in ROCm's success. See [[AMD]].
- **🆕 The AMD deal's capital structure — $5B of AMD's own CASH into Anthropic, not warrants (SemiAnalysis "Can AMD break the CUDA Moat? AMD Advancing AI 2026", 2026-07-24).** SemiAnalysis's read of the 2026-07-22 announcement adds the piece missing from the AMD-roundtable and BofA versions already on this page: alongside the **up-to-2GW of Instinct MI455X** (first gigawatt online **1H27** in Helios rack-scale systems) and the multi-year engineering collaboration pointing Claude at ROCm, **"AMD is investing up to $5B of its own cash into Anthropic, released as deployment milestones are met."** That is **equity flowing INTO Anthropic**, structurally the opposite of the OpenAI and Meta arrangements, where AMD issued each of them **performance warrants for up to 160M shares (~10% of shares out) at a $0.01 strike** vesting against 6GW of Instinct purchases — i.e. OpenAI and Meta are being *paid to buy* (SemiAnalysis models an effective rebate of ~$16.0B/GW at a $600 hurdle, ~105%/~85% discounts respectively), while Anthropic is being *invested in*. Read: Anthropic negotiated cash on its own balance sheet rather than a purchase rebate, consistent with a lab that is FCF-positive and pre-IPO rather than one needing its compute subsidised. Second structural point: **with AMD, Anthropic "is now set to run all four major accelerator platforms: Nvidia, TPUs, Trainium, and AMD"** — the page has been tracking these as five silicon *avenues* (incl. the Broadcom XPU design track and its own early-stage ASIC); SemiAnalysis's four-*platform* framing is the cleaner statement of what is genuinely differentiated here, since no other lab runs more than two at scale. That breadth is a real negotiating lever on every one of them. Evidence the porting cost is now low enough to make it credible: **Anthropic Head of Compute Tom Brown** described using **Claude over a single weekend with "/goal" to bring up Anthropic's internal Claude inference stack on AMD hardware** — the concrete datapoint behind SemiAnalysis upgrading AMD from "0% chance" (2024) to "non-zero" (AMD 2.0) to **"a great chance of success"**, and the sharper version of the Tom Brown "past the CUDA moat days" line logged above. Provenance note: SemiAnalysis had **predicted the AMD-Anthropic pairing in an April-2026 institutional note** from its Accelerator & HBM team (and on X on 07-20) — i.e. a scored forecast, not a reaction. See [[AMD]], [[NVDA]], [[AMZN]], [[GOOG]]. [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_24_ENC_Can_AMD_break_the_CUDA_Moat_AMD_Advancing_AI_2026_email.html)
- **🆕 READ-THROUGH — the 2GW commitment is now on an AMD EARNINGS CALL, with the 1H27 first-gigawatt timing intact, and Su volunteered the delivery path: THROUGH CSPs, NOT SELF-BUILD (AMD Q2 2026 earnings call, Bloomberg LIVE TRANSCRIPT, 2026-08-04).** The 2GW / 1H27 shape is already on this page from the 07-22 announcement and the 07-23 roundtable; what is net-new is **(a) AMD reaffirming it in prepared remarks on a reported quarter — the first time it carries earnings-call standing rather than event standing — and (b) how Su described the ramp mechanics.** Verbatim, prepared remarks: _"we announced a new strategic partnership with Anthropic. **Anthropic will deploy UP TO TWO GIGAWATTS of MI450-series GPUs in Helios, with deployment of the FIRST GIGAWATT BEGINNING IN THE FIRST HALF OF 2027.** The partnership includes a multi-year joint engineering collaboration using Claude to optimize workloads for Instinct GPUs and accelerate ROCm software development."_ ★ **The delivery-path detail is the genuinely new thing, and it changes how the commitment should show up in a model.** In Q&A, Su named **"our strategic anchor customers in OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic — they are ALL IN THE PROCESS OF RAMPING,"** and described that ramp as **"very much aligning their data center build outs and their work with their CLOUD SERVICE PROVIDERS, together with our ramp"** — i.e. **Anthropic's AMD capacity is expected to land THROUGH CSPs rather than through Anthropic-owned build.** Asked separately (Jim Schneider, GS) about MI450 customer diversity, Su was explicit: the frontier labs **"will be consuming through a number of CSPs… both hyperscalers and others."** ⚠️ **Read: the 2GW is a compute commitment, not necessarily an Anthropic-leased-datacenter commitment — consistent with the multi-cloud/fungible posture this page already carries, and it means the capacity may appear inside a CSP's capex and RPO rather than Anthropic's own. It also makes CSP data-center readiness, not AMD silicon, the gating variable on the 1H27 start.** Two supporting items from the same call: **rocm.ai "lets developers use today's leading coding agents, including Claude, Codex and Cursor, to create port and optimize code for Instinct"** (the productised form of the reciprocal engineering leg already on this page), and AMD is **"working closely with the leading AI labs, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and others to optimize ROCm for their models."** Finally, a mild dilution of the "frontier labs are the whole story" framing: Su flagged **"lots of customers who are interested in Helios at a more regular scale than gigawatt scale"** — i.e. AMD expects real non-frontier Helios diversity, which slightly reduces Anthropic's negotiating uniqueness on that platform. ⚠️ Machine transcript — product names normalised (MI450-series, ROCm, rocm.ai, EPYC); no garbled token quoted. - **BACKFILL / HISTORICAL — where Anthropic stood in Sept-2025, and the structural claim that has held up best (SemiAnalysis "Amazon's AI Resurgence: AWS & Anthropic's Multi-Gigawatt Trainium Expansion", Ontiveros/Patel/Kourabi/Xie, 2025-09-03 — ingested 2026-07-24, ~11 months old; supersedes nothing current on this page):** the Sep-2025 baseline, useful mostly as the origin point for the curves the rest of this page tracks. **Revenue $1B → $5B annualised during 2025 (5x YTD)**; the **~$13B round at a $183B valuation** (vs $965B post-money today). Crucially for the cloud-mix debate: **as of Q2-2025 Anthropic's cloud spend was still "over 2x smaller than that of OpenAI,"** and a large share of it was going to **Google Cloud** — Anthropic's early investor ($300M round in late-2022) and preferred cloud through 2023–24 before the expanded AWS deal — with SemiAnalysis believing **most of Anthropic's *inference* was served by Google Cloud on TPU** ("having the world's best inference system (TPU) is a key competitive advantage"). That is the direct ancestor of the 07-13 Archera read on this page (majority of Claude production PTU tokens still sold through Google Vertex) — the Google-inference tilt is an 18-month-old structural fact, not a 2026 development. AWS-relationship chronology as SemiAnalysis lays it out: **$1.25B (expandable to $4B) in Sept-2023**, expanded **March-2024** with the Trainium/Inferentia commitment, then **a further $4B in Nov-2024** naming AWS the primary LLM training partner. **The structural claim worth keeping — and the one that has aged best: "Trainium2 is converging toward an Anthropic custom-silicon program."** Anthropic was already "heavily involved in all Trainium design decisions" and "essentially use[s] Amazon's Annapurna Labs as a custom silicon partner," making it — **alongside Google DeepMind, the only two AI labs benefiting from tight hardware-software co-design.** Read forward: that framing anticipated by ~10 months both the 07-02 Information report of Anthropic's own early-stage chip and the 07-14 Samsung-Foundry engagement already logged above; the co-design thesis is the through-line. Mechanism given at the time: Trainium2 loses to GB200 on nearly every spec (3.85x FP16 FLOPs, 2.75x memory bandwidth, 3.1x aggregate scale-up bandwidth) but wins on **TCO per million tokens and TCO per TB/s of memory bandwidth** — and Anthropic's roadmap is "more memory-bandwidth-bound than FLOPs bound" because it is "the most aggressive AI Lab on scaling post-training techniques like Reinforcement Learning." Anthropic's ramp was expected to make it not only the sole large external Trainium2 user but **materially larger than Amazon's own internal needs (Bedrock, Alexa, etc.)**. **Product/moat as called then:** Claude Opus 4.1 led SWE-Bench and Claude remained "the top model in Cursor" against GPT-5 ("we see Cursor as the ultimate indicator of which model nails the balance between capability and usability"); the coding position was already framed as **creating a data moat and a flywheel effect** that OpenAI's tighter-privacy Copilot base could not replicate — the origin of the coding-flywheel argument the 07-09 note later grounded in RL-environment data buying. Risk named even then, and unchanged: **"lower network effects and entry barriers compared to ChatGPT's consumer moat"** — which SemiAnalysis argued "likely makes Anthropic more paranoid than any other lab." Ecosystem datapoint for the adoption curve Anthropic was riding: **Cursor took 750 days to $100M ARR, then broke $250M in 45 days and $500M in 15 days.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2025_09_03_ENC_Amazons_AI_Resurgence_AWS_Anthropics_Multi-Gigawatt_Trainium_Expansion_email.html)
- **Amazon partnership renegotiated — token-based billing (Rothschild & Co, TMT Daily sales, 2026-06-30 / 2026-07-01 detail).** Anthropic has renegotiated its Amazon partnership: **starting next year Amazon will be billed based on tokens processed rather than compute hours**, materially raising Amazon's AI costs — the concrete mechanic behind the 06-30 "flexing pricing power over Amazon" framing already on this page. This is prompting some Amazon engineers to **"distill" Anthropic models ahead of the change** (a defensive move to reduce dependence before the cost step-up lands). Amazon relies on Anthropic for **Alexa shopping, the Kiro coding tool, and the Quick workspace assistant**, and will evaluate cheaper alternatives including its in-house **Nova models** as it reassesses the relationship under the new billing structure (Rothschild & Co TMT Daily, sales, 2026-06-30).
- **Distillation-guardrails spreading to a second megacap customer (Rothschild & Co, 2026-06-30).** Separate from the Amazon dynamic, **Meta is restricting its engineers' use of Anthropic's Claude Code** (alongside OpenAI's Codex) within its applied-AI engineering division over "distillation" concerns; the policy has been in place since May 2026 — i.e. two of Anthropic's largest enterprise/hyperscaler counterparties are now independently guarding against model distillation by their own staff (Rothschild & Co TMT Daily, sales, 2026-06-30).
- **Anthropic goes on the offensive on "distillation attacks" against the Chinese labs — an IP/moat defense (BofA · Brian Fenske, 2026-07-17).** As Kimi K3 landed, BofA resurfaced Anthropic's escalating public stance: Anthropic has **publicly accused Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek and Minimax of "distillation attacks"** — illicitly extracting Claude's capabilities to train their own models. Its **Feb 23 2026 blog ("Detecting and preventing distillation attacks")** claimed industrial-scale campaigns (**Minimax ~13M exchanges the most; Moonshot/Kimi ~3.4M via hundreds of fraudulent accounts** attributed by request-metadata to senior Moonshot staff, later attempting to reconstruct Claude's reasoning traces); on **Jun 24 2026** Anthropic sent a letter to US officials calling an Alibaba effort "**the largest known distillation attack on Anthropic to date**." FinTwit corroboration (@PatrickMoorhead / @zephyr_z9): **Kimi K3 appears to have distilled Fable** (unbanned Jul 1), "so big training infra is still required for the leading edge." Read: reframes the "cheap Chinese open models" narrative as partly derivative of US-frontier output, and is Anthropic's active defense of its capability moat — but also underscores the leakage risk (why customers like Meta guard Claude Code internally, above). Vital Knowledge separately notes SpaceX's xAI reportedly selling excess compute to external customers including **Google and Anthropic**, drawing a parallel to Meta's newly-announced "Meta Compute" external-cloud pivot the same day (Vital Knowledge / Adam Crisafulli, 2026-07-01).

This converts what was previously an inference (StoneX/TrendForce, 06-23: the Micron/SK Hynix/Samsung HBM-in-2028 memory deals *imply* an own ASIC, since you only need HBM if you build/buy accelerators) into direct reporting. Separately, **Claude Opus 4.7 was the only model ranking top-5 in both volume usage and spending on OpenRouter in June 2026** (JPMorgan, Data Center Watch / Joseph Cardoso et al., 2026-07-01).

Cuts both ways: confirms Anthropic's pricing leverage but flags counterparty substitution risk at its largest equity backer/primary cloud.

A governance/policy contrast relevant to the Gurley/@Hesamation "lobbying-for-protection" debate.

- **Developer-platform architecture & roadmap — the "three-layer cake" (Anthropic @ Sequoia fireside — platform leads Caitlin & Angela, 2026-07-14):** the clearest first-party articulation of how Anthropic productizes Claude for builders (internal + external, deliberately kept the same primitives). Three ascending abstraction layers: **(1) knowledge** — the messages API + standards (MCP, skills, memory) that expose how the model thinks/does tool-calls; **(2) execution** — a low-level harness + managed infrastructure, today's high-level product being **Claude Managed Agents** (spawns governed sandboxes, stores/resumes transcript sessions, handles prompt-caching/context-window management out of the box); **(3) coordination** — the emerging layer of **"strategies"/meta-harnesses** built on the thesis that "tokens aren't fungible — a token has a job" (advising vs executing vs reflecting-to-memory vs best-of-n verification), which the roadmap is now moving toward. Design choices: not "precious" about running on Anthropic infra — **self-hosted sandboxes partnered with Modal, Vercel, Cloudflare and Amazon's new micro-VMs**, plus **MCP tunnels** to reach MCP servers behind a firewall. Verticalization is explicit (**finance, legal**) and biased to **token-hungry** use-cases (coding the archetype — "you finish a turn and want to do more"). Products framed as packagings of the same primitives: **Claude tag** (an "org-level harness" accessed via Slack — "the interface can swap, the context engineering underneath is the moat"), **Claude for financial services** (skills packages), **Claude design** (code-as-the-medium for generative design). On models: explicitly **not building a cross-vendor router — designing the platform for Claude only** (harnesses should be tuned to the model family, echoing Vercel's harness-agent approach). [tokenmaxxing](themes/tokenmaxxing.md). [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_14_anth_on_sequoia_14_jul_26.html)
- **"Token maxxing → token rationalization" — Anthropic's own framing (Anthropic @ Sequoia fireside, 2026-07-14):** asked about the shift from token-maxxing to rationalization, the platform team endorsed it as a "normal, natural cycle" — as models get more capable, the next optimization dimension after intelligence is **cost or speed**. Their guidance to enterprises: **don't stop AI usage** (the wrong move; often the spend erupted via "shadow IT" as employees installed Claude Code themselves) — instead design a **complexity-router strategy** (assess task complexity → route hard tasks to a big model, easy tasks to cheaper models), which Anthropic intends to offer as one of its composable "strategies" **within the Claude model family**. Corroborates the model-layer down-tiering pressure in the token-optimization bear reads on the page, but reframed as a within-Claude routing opportunity Anthropic wants to own rather than a share loss. [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_14_anth_on_sequoia_14_jul_26.html)
- **Channel share + capacity read — Claude ~70/30 over GPT, but served mostly off Google TPU (Archera expert call — ex-AWS operator, 2026-07-13):** an ex-AWS operator's book puts **client interest at ~70/30 Claude:GPT** (down from more Claude-dominant after the GPT-5.5 resurgence), with Claude having won the codegen use-case and the enterprise long-tail first (buyers procure it inside their VPC via Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry for data-privacy, not direct). Key capacity nuance: as of start-2026 **the majority of Claude production PTU tokens are sold through Google Vertex** — Google's deep TPU well can serve even leading-edge Opus/Fable, whereas **Sonnet runs fine on AWS Trainium2 but Opus 4.28/Fable show capacity issues on Amazon** (so Amazon still serves those off Nvidia GPUs, making its Claude token supply less fungible than Google's). Two bear flags: (1) **open-source competition — GLM 5.2** has hit the RL loop that made Opus special and, at ~¼ the cost, could over time squeeze the labs' codegen token share "down into 20%"; (2) enterprises are **wary of Anthropic's "propensity to compete with its partners,"** pushing them to keep an owned open-source model in a router alongside Claude. [tokenmaxxing](themes/tokenmaxxing.md). [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_13_archera_13_jul_26.html)
- **IPO financials sneak-peek — >$60B ARR, 3Q26 profit >$1B, $6T base case (SemiAnalysis "Anthropic 3Q26 Profit Over $1B", 2026-07-08).** SemiAnalysis's Tokenomics team (bottoms-up by SKU/tier/customer, "confirmed" by a recent WSJ piece) frames the confidential Jun-1 IPO filing: Anthropic ended 2025 at **$9B ARR → $30B by 1Q26** (Jan +$3B, Feb +$7B, Mar +$11B) → **>$60B today (3Q26)** — the first AI lab of this scale to IPO. **3Q26 GAAP EBIT ~$1B (6% margin)** vs OpenAI at ~−100% EBIT margin (Anthropic likely "does not want to be profitable" but compute constraints cap reinvestment). **Revenue mix: usage-based API 75–85% of revenue; subscriptions just 15% of ARR; only ~5% from Consumer subs (vs OpenAI ~40%).** Cumulative training cost of ~$8B since 1Q24 yielded a $60B ARR business (an "extremely impressive ROIC"). **NRR ~500%** (Krishna Rao on Invest Like the Best): of the $30B 1Q26 ARR, ~$12B came from customers present ≥1yr prior who were ~$2B in 1Q25 → **~$18B of new-customer ARR still ramping**; **NNARR now $10B+/month** (Fable the next accelerant, targeting >$10B/mo in 2H26). **Free MAUs ~55–60M, 9% of consumer MAUs paying** (vs OpenAI ~950M WAU, ~6% paying); Claude Code **>7% of total GitHub commits** — the driver of the 1Q26 reacceleration. Plans $20/$100/$200/mo; **avg paying US consumer ~$45/mo** (card-panel). Unit-econ detail: **blended inference GM mid-60s% (vs −94% in 2024); Opus 4.8 API-token GM 80%+; ARR-per-MW reaching ~$60M later this year vs ~$16M 9 months ago; 2Q26 EBTIT margin ~36%.** ≥60% of compute is earmarked for training/internal today; long-run ~25% of revenue on training compute (48%/52% training/inference split by 2030). Steady-state 30–40% EBIT/FCF margins possible (GM into mid-70s). >$100B raised. **Base-case valuation 20x 2027 ending-ARR of $300B (~$15B/mo NNARR in 2027) → ~$6T EV, the world's largest company** — "Anthropic as the first $6T company as a base-case." Compute is the governor: SemiAnalysis sees OpenAI+Anthropic >100GW of unconstrained demand by 2030 (>90GW of net adds through 2030 vs 2.5GW in 2025 / 5GW in 2026; ~6GW available today) — the IPO's purpose is capital access to bid up compute. Risk flagged: more Fable-style government delays (regulatory lock-in doesn't help when hyperscaler labs are catching up + Chinese labs distilling) (SemiAnalysis "Anthropic 3Q26 Profit Over $1B: The Anthropic IPO Financials Sneak Peak", Brookhart/Huang/Patel, 2026-07-08). Token-spend optimization ("value maxing") is now a majority-of-enterprises concern installing controls (Cursor: "every single customer conversation is about this now"), and the dominant lever is routing non-frontier tasks to cheaper open-source models (GLM/Z.ai, Kimi/Moonshot, DeepSeek, Qwen/Alibaba) — "the first few potential dents to the revenue growth trajectories of the Frontier Labs."
