Read: a genuine speed-bump on the *durability/quality* of Anthropic's reported ARR growth, not (yet) a demand break — consistent with SemiAnalysis "TokenBudgeting" (06-30: "not a material risk to 2H26 AI budgets") and the within-Claude complexity-router reframing Anthropic itself offered (07-14 Sequoia fireside). Semis/hyperscaler read-through on [tokenmaxxing](themes/tokenmaxxing.md). (UBS, 2026-07-22) [../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_22_ubs_open_source_models_and_token_spend_optimizatio.html](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_22_ubs_open_source_models_and_token_spend_optimizatio.html)
- **★ THE FIRST AUDITED THIRD-PARTY MARK ON ANTHROPIC EQUITY ANYWHERE ON THIS PAGE — Microsoft booked a $3.2 BILLION GAIN on its Anthropic investment in its June quarter (MSFT 4QFY26 earnings call, 2026-07-29).** Amy Hood, verbatim: _"Several discrete items impacted our financial results in the quarter when compared to our forward-looking guidance provided on our April earnings call, resulting in a benefit of **$0.27 on diluted earnings per share**. These included a **$3.2 billion gain from our investment in Anthropic** and lower-than-expected expenses related to the voluntary retirement program, which were partially offset by severance expense and impairment charges in Xbox."_ And on the line it lands in: _"When adjusted for the impact of our investments in OpenAI, **other income and expense was $2.8 billion, driven by the gain on investment in Anthropic** noted earlier."_ **Why this matters on a private name: every valuation datapoint on this page — the $965B Series H post-money, the ~$900bn tender chatter, PitchBook's lagging $396bn estimate — is a primary-round or secondary-market print. This is the first time a public, SEC-reporting counterparty has put a REALISED-IN-EARNINGS number on the appreciation of an Anthropic stake, in an audited quarter, and sized it materially enough to be a named discrete item and roughly the largest single component of a Mag-7 EPS beat.** ⚠️ **DO NOT BACK OUT AN IMPLIED VALUATION FROM IT — the call does not support one.** Microsoft disclosed **no stake size, no cost basis, no carrying value, no accounting method (fair-value vs equity-method vs measurement-alternative remeasurement), and no trigger** for the gain. The only reference point already on this page for what Microsoft put in is Nomura's reprise of the **Nov-2025 Nvidia/Microsoft tie-up: "NVDA up to USD10bn + MSFT up to USD5bn into Anthropic"** alongside the up-to-1GW GB/VR Azure arrangement (Nomura "Is the cycle over", 2026-06-30) and JPM's **"Azure up to 1 GW initially ($30B compute commitment)"** (JPM "AI Capex 2.0", 2026-06-16). **Against a committed ceiling of ~$5bn, a $3.2bn single-quarter gain is very large in proportional terms** — but the honest statement of what is known is that the gain is **large relative to the size of Microsoft's disclosed commitment and consistent in direction with the round progression this page already carries (Series G $380B post, Feb-26 → Series H $965B post, May-26, ~2.5x)**, and nothing more. Two further cautions: (a) MSFT's fiscal Q4 ran **Apr-1 → Jun-30 2026**, which straddles the **28-May-2026 Series H close** — so a round-driven remeasurement is the most obvious candidate, meaning the gain may be **marking to a round this page already knows about rather than revealing a newer one**; (b) it is a **non-cash mark, not a realisation**. **Reconciled against prior wiki comments only (private name — no BBG, no house model): nothing on this page is superseded.** The Series H $965B post-money stands as the last known valuation; this is corroborating, independent, audited evidence that a public holder marked its position **up** in the June quarter — which is a modest counterweight to the one bearish item on this page, the unverified TickerTrends read that "**Anthropic ARR sequential growth has slowed significantly**" (Rothschild/Adley, 07-24), though note a balance-sheet mark and an ARR trajectory are different objects and the mark most likely reflects the May round rather than June operating trends. (MSFT 4QFY26 earnings call, 2026-07-29) [Transcript](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Microsoft_Corp_Earnings_Call_2026729_DN000000003114409501pdf.html)
- **★ Claude's distribution inside Microsoft, sized by Microsoft — and in the same breath, Microsoft's first quantified attack on an Anthropic product (MSFT 4QFY26 earnings call, 2026-07-29).** **The distribution win, confirmed at the top of Nadella's platform section:** Azure offers _"the broadest model catalog in the cloud with **over 11,000 models**, including the latest from OpenAI, **Anthropic**, Mistral, X-AI as well as our own MAI family,"_ and — the successor to the "10,000+ Foundry customers using >1 model, up 2x q/q" mark this page carries from MSFT IR (2026-05-18) — _"**Since the start of the year, we have seen 5x increase in the number of customers building with models from multiple providers.**"_ The named reference account is a joint OpenAI-plus-Anthropic build: _"**Levi Strauss & Co**, for example, is using models from OpenAI and Anthropic on Foundry as it brings **more than 1,000 domain-specific agents** into a unified enterprise AI platform."_ Nadella's stated architecture is explicitly substitution-friendly — _"the harness, context, memory, and action space are separate from any one model family… **every model is substitutable**"_ — and he cites the **Hugging Face incident** as the resilience argument for multi-model (_"you can't be subject to the refusals of one model"_). **Read alongside the UBS 07-26 row already on this page: Anthropic is a scored SHARE GAINER in knowledge work through the Microsoft channel, and multi-provider adoption is compounding — but the channel owner is also the gatekeeper, and it just showed why.** ⚠️ **The competitive item, and it is the first time a counterparty has put a number on beating Mythos:** in security, _"**MAI, Cyber 1 Flash achieves better performance than much larger Mithos [Mythos] model, but at half the cost when combined with our multi-agent security harness**"_ — with Nadella supplying the mechanism later in Q&A: _"we proved with the **MDASH data in Cybergym** that essentially you can have those level performance with **50% less cost** because of this MAI cyber Flash one. And the reason is because **90% of the tasks are done by the Cyber Flash One model and 10% of the tasks you still go to the frontier**."_ **This upgrades the 07-27 row on this page (The Information framing Project Perception as "a cheaper alternative to Anthropic's Mythos") from press characterisation to a first-party claim with a cost figure and a routing ratio** — and note the structure of the claim is not "our model is better," it is **"90% of the work does not need the frontier"**, which is the cheap-model-plus-harness substitution thesis pointed directly at Anthropic's highest-value, unreleased product. Microsoft made the same claim shape against OpenAI in the same script (MAI Code 1 Flash at GPT-5.6-comparable quality in Excel for less; ~10% lower median token usage in GitHub Copilot while still routing to _"Frontier capabilities from OpenAI and Anthropic"_) — so read it as a **platform-wide token-cost-reduction programme that Anthropic is on the wrong side of as a supplier and the right side of as a catalog participant**, not as an Anthropic-specific attack. Nadella's framing of the underlying incentive is unusually blunt for a partner: enterprises should keep _"their human capital and their token capital"_ and _"the models are an input, not some extraction of the knowledge of the enterprise."_ ⚠️ Unverified/unaddressed on the call: whether Anthropic's Azure compute arrangement (up to 1GW / ~$30B per JPM) was expanded, and any Claude-token revenue figure through Foundry — Microsoft gave neither. (MSFT 4QFY26 earnings call, 2026-07-29)

- **BACKFILL / HISTORICAL — the ORIGIN of the TPU-vs-Trainium mix debate this page still tracks (FUNDA "Preview\|AWS 3Q25: AWS Acceleration Ahead, but TRN3 Remains the Key", 2025-10-28 — NINE MONTHS OLD, supersedes nothing, and no 2025 figure here should be read against a 2026 one).** FUNDA's Oct-2025 AWS preview, built on named data-center and AI-lab expert checks, is the earliest clean statement of why Anthropic's silicon mix ended up where it is. **On training: "Anthropic migrating training from GPU to TRN2, planning to use Project Rainer's 600k TRN2 chips to train 'Claude 4+', but currently only 3.5 Haiku successfully completed training on TRN2 — opus 3.5 [and] sonnet 3.5 both failed."** i.e. as of Oct-2025 the Trainium2 training programme had one shipped model to show for it, at the smallest tier. **On inference: "AWS is trying to get Anthropic to use TRN2 for inference but it's challenging… Haiku runs inference on Trn2, but currently Anthropic's inference remains predominantly on TPU. GCP is also pushing Anthropic to use TPU for training."** **On why — the mechanism that has aged best: "Anthropic originally wrote in jax, which is more TPU-compatible, so when urgently needing compute they'll definitely prioritize TPU. TRN2 still has debugging issues, so new inference capacity will prioritize TPU,"** with an AI-lab technical expert adding that "TRN's software stack is inferior to TPU" and that TRN3 may fix scale-up while software takes longer. Supporting context from the same note: FUNDA modelled TRN2 at a "neutral ~40% utilization" assumption on the view that TRN2 "essentially cannot handle training and will likely be used primarily for inference and reinforcement learning," and flagged **Anthropic's heavy TPU inference use as crowding out TRN2/TRN3 demand**. ⚠️ **Why it is worth carrying: this is the direct ancestor of two live items on this page — the Archera read (07-13) that the majority of Claude production PTU tokens are still sold through Google Vertex, and the SemiAnalysis Sep-2025 backfill that most of Anthropic's inference was served on Google TPU. The Google-inference tilt is a 2023-2025 structural fact, not a 2026 development, and it scored well: the JAX/TPU-priority prediction is exactly what the 2026 flow shows.** ⚠️ **Source caveat: this PDF is a print-to-PDF with the right margin clipped on several lines — some sentences end mid-word. Only complete fragments are quoted above; nothing has been reconstructed.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Preview_AWS_3Q25__AWS_Acceleration_Ahead_but_TRN3_Remains_the_Key.html)

## Debate / thesis
- **Bull:** Enterprise + coding leadership is real and compounding — #1 US business share (Ramp, 2026-06-18); Claude Code is the sticky agentic harness that won the coding workflow from Cursor/Copilot; token-based API economics are profitable and AI spend is the fastest-growing cost category Ramp has ever tracked (+15x Jan-2025→May-2026). Frontier value accrual is decisive — frontier models capture ~90% of economic value even as open-source captures the majority of tokens (BG2Pod, 2026-06-12). The coding edge is structurally rooted: Anthropic was among the earliest (1H-2024) to scale **synthetic data for coding/agent training** and ran a low-multimodal, coding/agent-heavy pretraining mix — yielding a durable token-efficient lead that suits enterprise (stability/cost > peak benchmarks) (FundaAI LLM note, 2026-01-28). Safety brand is a feature for regulated enterprises, and the **mission-driven culture is a talent moat** — ~80% retention, with employees ~8x more likely to leave OpenAI and ~11x more likely to leave DeepMind for Anthropic than vice versa (JPM initiation, 2025-09-18). JPM sized a **$635bn+ 2030 TAM** ($400bn+ enterprise, $235bn+ consumer). The Fable-5/DoD "supply-chain risk" episodes paradoxically *accelerated* adoption (Big Technology, 2026-06-18).
- **Bear:** **Capital intensity / compute cost** — chronic compute constraints cause persistent outages ("models down all the time"); Mythos can't be served economically (Allen Roush, 2026-04-28; Big Technology, 2026-06-18). The forced multi-cloud pivot shows compute is "physical power" shaped by contract terms and supply chain, not an abstract input (FundaAI, 2026-01-28). **Competition** — GPT-5.5 has closed most of the gap with Opus at the top; Google is the underrated cost-control winner; xAI/SpaceX + Cursor data is a credible new frontier-coding entrant (BG2Pod, 2026-06-12). **Pricing outlier** — at the Sep-25 snapshot Claude Opus 4.1 API was ~8x pricier than similarly performant Google/OpenAI models ($15/$75 per MTok vs ~$1.25/$10), with cheap Chinese models (GLM-4.5 ~64x cheaper, Kimi K2, Qwen 3) and DeepSeek pressuring the premium; OpenAI's GPT-5 had displaced Claude as Cursor's default (JPM initiation, 2025-09-18). **Customer concentration** — JPM/The Information flagged ~24% of revenue (~$1.2bn) from just 2 customers (likely Cursor + GitHub Copilot) (JPM initiation, 2025-09-18). **Model substitution / token-cost control** — enterprises increasingly route to cheaper/open-source models; neither Anthropic nor OpenAI offer spend-management controls, the #1 enterprise complaint (Big Technology, 2026-06-18). **Litigation** — the ~$1.5bn author-copyright settlement (~20% of ARR at the time; Bartz v. Anthropic) plus the Reddit data-scraping suit (JPM initiation, 2025-09-18). **Tokenmaxxing** overhang — alleged Amazon "tokenmaxxing" to pad Claude ARR (~$500M mystery bill) raises ARR-quality questions (@zerohedge via AMZN roll-up, `_briefings`).
- **Morgan Stanley (Byrd): quality frontier tokens justify premium, ~$55 ROI on $2-3 token spend (2026-06-26).** MS's Head of Thematic Research gives a concrete enterprise ROI example: a **6,000-line program coded with a premium tool (Anthropic-tier) for $58 ($1 per 100 lines)**, saving thousands of dollars and days of work vs. cheaper alternatives where errors erode cost savings. Enterprise average case: **save ~$55 on $2-3 in tokens** ($5/million tokens, a few hundred thousand tokens/use case). Core argument: "A token is not a token is not a token" — quality and embedded intelligence of frontier American models command a durable premium for complex, mission-critical enterprise workloads. US/Western enterprises show "significant concern about security risks with Chinese models, preferring Western alternatives." MS stays positive on frontier model developers (Anthropic, OpenAI) as entities capturing value even as open-source/Chinese models gain share in the long tail. Caveat: if orchestration layers can effectively "cobble together" multiple cheaper models to match frontier output, commoditization risk is real — "the jury is out on this." Net: bull for enterprise segment, mixed on commoditization risk (Morgan Stanley / Stephen Byrd "Discussion on tokenmaxxing", 2026-06-26). [../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_06_26_stephen_byrd_on_tokenmaxxing.html](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_06_26_stephen_byrd_on_tokenmaxxing.html)
- **Mixed (token-optimization read-through):** UBS's enterprise "token-maxxing" work cuts both ways for Anthropic. The structural risk is model-layer **down-tiering** — enterprises routing to cheaper/open-source models to control token costs, the chief pressure on frontier-lab API revenue. But the same checks repeatedly cite **heavy use of Anthropic Claude**, and notably that "you can actually get away with using Anthropic Sonnet for a lot of" engineering work cost-effectively (with Opus 4.8 reserved for the hardest jobs) — i.e. Sonnet is a favored cost-efficient workhorse, a relative usage positive even as API pricing faces broad pressure (UBS "The Ramp in Token Optimization" / Arcuri-Keirstead, 2026-06-23).
- **SaaS-displacement optionality vs counterparty-substitution risk (The Information / MS TMT / Bernstein TMT, 2026-07-06):** two-sided read from the same week. Bull: a report that **small firms are using Claude to replace Salesforce** — early directional evidence that agentic Claude workflows can substitute for packaged SaaS (CRM read-through), expanding the enterprise TAM beyond API tokens into application-layer displacement. Bear/nuance: at the megacap end, **Amazon is evaluating alternatives (OpenAI models, its own Nova) to reduce Claude dependence** after the token-based-billing renegotiation raised its costs — the same substitution dynamic now visible at Anthropic's largest backer, alongside the Meta Claude Code restriction (06-30). Net: Anthropic is displacing SaaS incumbents at the SMB end while its own hyperscaler counterparties guard against dependence at the top.
- **Claude Cowork is now the engine inside Microsoft's own agentic product, and UBS calls the partnership the right outcome — for Microsoft (UBS · Karl Keirstead / Taylor McGinnis / Jack Fyda "Microsoft Corp. — Update on Azure, Capex and M365", 2026-07-26):** the most consequential distribution datapoint on this page and, read carefully, a two-edged one. **The mechanic, stated plainly:** "Announced in March and GA in mid-June 2026, **Copilot Cowork enables Microsoft to leverage Anthropic's Claude Cowork harness natively inside Copilot.** Relative to Copilot's more single-step prompting and processing, Cowork can string together multi-step workflows autonomously across apps and context." **UBS's verdict on the partnership is explicit and is a compliment to Anthropic's execution speed rather than to Microsoft's:** "while we think a sizeable portion of investors viewed this decision as **an admission that Microsoft was behind in AI innovation and ought to have innovated more quickly rather than partner (forcing Microsoft to share the rents of Cowork)**, in our view, **Microsoft's decision to partner with Anthropic to launch the product was the best outcome for Microsoft given the pace of innovation at the model providers.**" Note the phrase "share the rents of Cowork" — that is the Anthropic economics, inside the largest productivity install base in the world. **Field evidence: partners like the engine, resist the meter.** Partner 2 — "It's still too early. **The excitement is that you can use Claude as the backend engine.** I think there's hesitation with consumption pricing." Partner 7 — "**The consumption piece is a non-starter. On top of the fixed $30 fee, customers don't see the value.**" Partner 1 priced a real task: pointing Cowork at 10-15 folders of documents and emails to build a brief "would have cost **6,500 credits, or $65**… if you think that saved 25 hours of work, then that's a great deal but it can spin up fast," and — the item that matters for the head-to-head — "**We haven't seen the cost analysis of Copilot Cowork vs Claude Cowork/ChatGPT yet.**" Customer 4 states the decision rule Anthropic will be judged on: "**If one's crazy more expensive than the other and they're technologically close, then the commercial side will win. If they're similar cost wise, they will come down to tech today.**" **Microsoft is simultaneously partner and gatekeeper, and Partner 2 documents the throttle:** "Cowork somewhat improves Microsoft's positioning. **Microsoft has also limited some of the functionality of what Anthropic Cowork can integrate into. You can integrate it into OneDrive to view documents but it can't create. You need to do that manually. But Copilot Cowork can create a document. It integrates into the security so that is an advantage.**" i.e. the first-party wrapper is deliberately privileged over Anthropic's own Cowork inside Microsoft's estate — the same posture as the Claude-agent-in-Teams item already on this page, now with a concrete capability restriction attached. **Anthropic scored a share gainer in knowledge work:** UBS's semi-annual Enterprise AI survey has M365 Copilot retaining mid-large-enterprise leadership "**despite share gains from OpenAI (via its new ChatGPT Work product) and Anthropic Claude (via Claude Cowork)**," with Google Gemini, Grok and Perplexity "los[ing] some ground" — and UBS's framing of the whole debate names Anthropic as one of the three rivals that "have stepped into the 'knowledge work' software arena." **The monetization layer beneath it:** "Azure as well as AWS and Google Cloud are now **materially monetizing OpenAI, Anthropic and Google model API access, as well as 1P product demand**," with the hyperscalers benefiting "from their role as **front-ends to the models and 1P products (such as Claude Code)**" — but the checks also show the channel being bypassed, Customer 9: "we need to be multi-model and are **now talking directly with Anthropic and OpenAI**." **Two bear datapoints, logged as found.** Customer 5, an oil & gas operator: "**We do not use Claude because we are not trying to trust more on Claude.** For an oil and gas company, we try to focus on using companies that have been a long time in the market and are stable" — vendor-longevity risk, an objection that no amount of model quality answers. And Partner 2 on the labs' economics: "**OpenAI and Anthropic are bleeding a ton of money**, so it would be very difficult" for them to displace Office. **The structural point Anthropic should like least:** UBS argues the consensus investor view is that "an AI model market dominated by three frontier lab giants (**Anthropic, OpenAI and Google**) creates risk for the hyperscalers, with too much economic power concentrated in too few customers, while a more diffuse and competitive multi-model market diminishes that risk" — and reads Satya's blog campaign (Jun-14 / Jul-12 / Jul-24) as Microsoft positioning itself explicitly against "the growing control/power of a few frontier AI model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI and Google)." Anthropic's largest new distribution partner is publicly campaigning to commoditize Anthropic's layer. _Private name — no BBG or house numbers to reconcile against; this is checked only against prior wiki commentary, which it corroborates on Cowork traction and extends on the Microsoft-throttling and cost-per-task points._ [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/ued48088.html)
- **Where ARR leadership stands:** Anthropic overtook OpenAI on ARR/business-share in May–Jun 2026 and is turning profitable; the live debate is durability vs frontier-substitution and whether compute supply can keep pace.
- **Secondary-market froth as a valuation risk (Barron's, 2026-05-25).** An institutional trader's characterization of the tender-offer scramble — signed-and-funded deadlines within days, "the f___ing wild, wild west" — plus SPV fee-stacking of "1.75% with a 20% carry" on a $200mm placement, is a soft signal that private-market valuation discovery for Anthropic is running hot/frictional ahead of any IPO print, a nuance for anyone marking the $900bn-$965bn range as clean. Governance context (Barron's "Other Voices," 2026-06-08): Anthropic and SpaceX are cited as the two megacap examples of new private companies raising capital near $1T valuations, out of ~1,680 unicorns PitchBook tracks, of which ~40% of aggregate value sits in AI firms — i.e. Anthropic's valuation risk is also a concentration/bubble-adjacent risk shared with a narrow set of AI megacaps.
- **Frenemy convergence — rivals now depend on one another (The Information, 2026-07-08):** xAI, Meta and Anthropic are increasingly moving into each other's core businesses (chips, models, data centers, customers) — the three are now structurally interdependent even as they compete. Cuts both ways: enlarges Anthropic's compute-supply and distribution surface (e.g. compute rented from xAI/SpaceX Colossus; Meta private-Claude talks) while sharpening the frontier-competition and counterparty-substitution risk already tracked on this page. (mixed; competicao)
- **Grok 4.5 pricing pressure at the frontier tier (Rothschild & Co, 2026-07-09):** SpaceXAI's newly launched Grok 4.5 claims Opus-4.8-adjacent quality at **$2/$6 per M input/output tokens (>60% cheaper than Opus 4.8 / GPT-5.5)** and 80 tokens/sec — a fresh price/perf challenger to Anthropic's frontier tier that feeds the model-substitution / ASP-compression bear case. (bear; competicao)
- **Frontier-AI pecking order — Anthropic on top (Vital Knowledge · Adam Crisafulli, 2026-07-11):** the market's frontier-AI ranking is now **Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Google, SpaceX**, with **Microsoft & Amazon "not really in the frontier-model conversation."** A bullish read placing Anthropic at #1 on the frontier leaderboard even as the substitution / ASP-compression bears (Grok 4.5 pricing, Chinese distillation) press from below. (bull; competicao)
- **🆕 Both ways — inside Copilot, Anthropic is the model Microsoft PAYS FOR, and that is simultaneously revenue and a routing liability (Microsoft IR/management fireside hosted by Jefferies (London), 2026-09-11 — MANAGEMENT source, not Jefferies research).** Microsoft, unprompted, gives the cost structure: *"if you're in co-pilot for example and you're using an OpenAI model, that's economically better than if they're using an Anthropic model **because we don't pay rents there**"* — Microsoft owns the OpenAI IP and pays no model rents on it, and pays rents on Claude. **Bull read:** Anthropic is collecting third-party model rents from the largest enterprise-productivity distribution channel in the market, which is exactly the kind of revenue an S-1 reader will want split out. **Bear read:** the distributor's gross margin improves every time the router picks a non-Anthropic model, Microsoft controls the router (*"you put on auto mode… let us route you to the model that makes the most sense"*), and the only stated counterweight is customer experience. ➜ **The test to run on the prospectus: how much of Anthropic's enterprise revenue arrives through channels whose owner is economically better off routing elsewhere.**
- **Bear — the open-model catch-up rate is now MEASURED, and it is HALVING every era (SemiAnalysis, "Are Open Models Catching Up?", 2026-08-21).** The commoditization bear stops being a vibe and becomes a rate: open models have taken half as long to catch the first closed model of each era (35.8-point initial gap in Era 1; 12.1 points closed in 8.5 months in Era 2; 4.8 months for Kimi K2.6 past Opus 4.5 and 6 months for GLM-5.2 past GPT-5.2 in Era 3), and SemiAnalysis states the consequence itself — if open models stay capable enough at a fraction of the cost the model layer commoditizes, which "would obviously be disastrous for frontier lab margins." **What makes it a live risk rather than a benchmark curiosity is the workload: the note says GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 are "genuinely capable of many of the same coding and agentic tasks" that produced the $65B+ ARR.** **Two offsets, from the same note:** (1) the PRODUCT gap closes slower than the BENCHMARK gap — SemiAnalysis itself prefers Fable over higher-scoring Kimi K3 for its own work, and credits Anthropic as "the first to nail a model + harness product"; (2) COMPUTE CONCENTRATION — frontier tokens at API prices earn as much as $100M per MW per year of REVENUE against sub-$30M for open-source TaaS / colo / legacy cloud, so the labs should out-bid open-weight labs for incremental compute even though Anthropic + [[OPENAI]] are only ~27% of 2026 net-new GW today. ⚠️ Scores are SemiAnalysis’s own normalised composites, not vendor-reported, and are not comparable across eras.
- **🆕 Mixed — THE HARNESS-AS-MOAT CLAIM NOW HAS FOUR DATED VOICES IN FOUR DAYS, AND THEY SPLIT BY SEAT (2026-09-08..11 — three Capstone Communacopia-week Notion transcripts plus the on-page [[MSFT]] primary).** FOR, from inside the company — Anthropic GTM LatAm FSI (Alvarenga @ BTG session, 2026-09-10, Capstone Notion transcript): *"the engine and… the other parts of the car"*, harness maturity *"six to seven"* out of ten, *"token efficiency when you have harness and model from the same company"*, and first-party app usage growing faster than the hyperscaler channel. FOR, from an independent — SemiAnalysis ('Max' @ client dinner, 2026-09-08, Capstone Notion transcript; **independent research, not a broker**): *"the person who creates the model also has the right to make the best harness for that particular model"*, and the wrappers have conceded it — *"Cursor, Cognition, Harvey… have all since realized that was sort of a fool's dream… Cognition is also training their own models now. Harvey is training their own models now"*, the Cursor founder paraphrased as *"my business is doomed if we don't actually make the best coding model."* SemiAnalysis adds a SECOND, separate moat — **RSI**: models *"are speeding up AI research at both OpenAI and Anthropic"* (visible in release cadence), and it is *"technically illegal"* for Google, Meta, SpaceX or Chinese labs to use those models to do that research. AGAINST, from a rival lab — MiniMax CEO (GS Communacopia fireside, 2026-09-09, Capstone Notion transcript): *"you will see all the top labs they designed their own harness… But… **people pay for the intelligence, people pay for the tokens**. So you can definitely bring your API key to whatever harness."* AGAINST, from the largest distributor — [[MSFT]] (09-11, bullet above): an integrated harness+model is *"never the world we thought would exist."* ➜ **Net for this page: the moat is asserted by the two parties who own a harness-and-model (Anthropic, and SemiAnalysis on its behalf) and denied by the two parties whose business depends on models being swappable (MiniMax sells tokens; Microsoft sells the router). The falsifiable version is the S-1 channel split — revenue through Anthropic's own surfaces versus Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry — which GTM says is tilting 1P and which Microsoft says it is economically motivated to tilt back.** ⚠️ **All three new voices are machine-transcribed, unlabeled-speaker Notion notes; SemiAnalysis is independent research, never a broker; MiniMax is not a covered name.** (mixed; competicao / produto)

## Intra-quarter — calls, commentary & reports (since the last print)
_intra-quarter · Apr 16 → Jul 29, 2026 · sell-side / expert calls / reports between earnings. Timeline visual: [timeline.html](timeline.html)._

**🆕🔴🔴🔴 2026-09-17 (ingest — document dated August 2026) — THE FIRST FRONTIER LAB TO PUT A *MEASURED, MONTHLY, DATED* NUMBER ON AI BUILDING AI: CLAUDE NOW "LEADS" **26% OF ANTHROPIC'S OWN MODEL R&D**, FROM ~0% IN FEBRUARY — AND THE COMPANY SIMULTANEOUSLY DISCLOSES **~30,000 CONCURRENT INTERNAL AGENTS** AND **OVER A BILLION MONITORED AGENT DECISIONS IN ONE MONTH**. THIS IS THE BEST DEMAND-SIDE PRIMARY THIS WIKI HAS ON THE RSI QUESTION, AND IT IS ALSO A SELF-REPORT GRADED BY THE COMPANY'S OWN MODEL.**

(**Anthropic** — *"Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs"*, anthropic.com/institute, **snapshot August 2026**, retrieved 2026-09-17. Marina Favaro & Phillie Wright; research direction **Jack Clark**; technical work by Jun Shern Chan, Brian Calvert, Francesco Mosconi, Henry de Valence, Fabien Roger, Joe Benton. Archived with full text + figure: [`20260800_Anthropic_Institute_Measuring_pace_of_AI_development_inside_frontier_labs.html`](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/20260800_Anthropic_Institute_Measuring_pace_of_AI_development_inside_frontier_labs.html).)

⚠️⚠️ **SOURCE-TYPE GUARD, APPLIED BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. This is a COMPANY SELF-REPORT BY A PRIVATE LAB ABOUT ITSELF** — first-party primary, closest in kind to management commentary on this wiki. **It is NOT research: no rating, no price target, no model, no estimates, and nothing here aggregates with rated notes.** Anthropic states the conflict itself — it is *"using our own models to evaluate our systems"* — and frames the whole exercise as a proposed disclosure standard under its **Advanced AI Framework (AAIF)**, i.e. it is partly advocacy for a regime in which labs self-report. Read it as a disclosure, not as an audit.

### 🔴🔴🔴 (1) THE AUTOMATION INDEX — AND THE MONTHLY SERIES IS *NOT IN THE BODY TEXT*, IT IS ONLY IN THE CHART

The prose gives one number (26%, August 2026). **The full trajectory exists only inside the figure image** — transcribed here, because the shape is the whole story:

| Anthropic R&D Automation Index v2026.07 — share of model R&D tasks at **AL4 "AI leads"** | | | | | | | |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Month (2026) | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Jul | **Aug** |
| AL4 share | ~0% | **1%** | **3%** | **12%** | **14%** | **22%** | **26%** |

_Aug-2025 through Feb-2026 all sit at ~0%. Vertical bars on the chart are 90% measurement intervals. Scale is Epoch AI's Automation Level: AL0 no AI · AL1 minimal · AL2 AI assists · AL3 AI collaborates · AL4 AI leads · AL5 fully automated._

- 🔴🔴🔴 **THE SHAPE IS NOT A SMOOTH EXPONENTIAL — IT IS TWO STEP-CHANGES SEPARATED BY PLATEAUS.** Mar→Apr **+2pp**, **Apr→May +9pp (4x in one month)**, May→Jun **+2pp**, **Jun→Jul +8pp**, Jul→Aug **+4pp**. ➤ **A series that jumps 4x in a month and then adds 2pp in the next is behaving like a step function keyed to model releases, not like a continuously compounding capability.** ⚠️ **THE RELEASE ATTRIBUTION IS MY INFERENCE, NOT ANTHROPIC'S — the document offers no explanation for the step timing and names no model version against any month. Logged as a pattern to test, not a mechanism to adopt.**
- 🔴🔴 **THE TWO BOUNDS THAT MATTER, BOTH FIRST-PARTY AND BOTH IN THE PROSE:** *"The share of work at or above 'AI collaborates' is above 90%"* — and, stated flatly, ***"Claude is not operating fully autonomously for any measured subset of AI R&D work."*** **AL5 is zero across the entire chart.** ➤ **So the honest summary is: near-total penetration at the assist/collaborate level, a quarter of tasks led, and nothing running unsupervised. The bear and the bull both have something here, and the page should carry both halves together.**

### ⚠️⚠️🔴 (2) THE CAVEAT THAT GOVERNS HOW MUCH WEIGHT THE 26% CAN TAKE — AND IT IS IN ANTHROPIC'S OWN METHODOLOGY

*"Our judge model agreed with humans about as often as humans agreed with each other (**model-versus-human exact agreement was 59%, human-versus-human was 35%**), and model and human ratings were within one level of each other **97%** of the time. There remains real room for disagreement on borderline cases, such as where exactly 'AI collaborates' ends and 'AI leads' begins."*

➤ **Anthropic presents the 59%-vs-35% comparison as reassurance — the judge is no worse than a human. Read the other way, it is the sharpest limitation in the document: humans agree with each other on the exact automation level only about a third of the time. The AL3/AL4 boundary is precisely where the headline "26% leads" is cut.** ⚠️ **Practical consequence for this wiki: treat the LEVEL as soft (the 97%-within-one-level figure is the honest precision) and the DIRECTION and SLOPE as the informative content. A 26% that could plausibly be argued as high-AL3 does not change the fact that it was ~0% six months earlier.**

### 🔴🔴 (3) THE FROZEN BASKET — AND, TO ANTHROPIC'S CREDIT, THEY TESTED THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION

*"Second, the basket is frozen. A growing index number on a July 2026 baseline tells us that the work humans were doing **at that time** is being automated; it does not, on its own, tell us whether new kinds of work are appearing that humans have shifted onto."*

**The natural attack on any such index is that a frozen basket mechanically drifts toward higher automation as the work moves on. Anthropic pre-empted it:** *"we constructed an alternate version of the frozen tree from January 2026 data, and compared new tasks arriving every month from February to July 2026 against that January 2026 basket. **We found no rise in the number of 'novel' tasks** between the January and July baskets of tasks, suggesting that the structure of model R&D work is stable at our level of analysis."* They also commit to *"rebuild the basket of tasks periodically and re-version our published automation numbers."*

⚠️ **AND THE PART THEY DO NOT FLAG, WHICH IS A REAL WEIGHTING ARTEFACT: the index is person-time weighted as *"Each person gets one unit of weight per week, split evenly across the tasks they worked on that week. If person A worked on four tasks, each gets 0.25; if person B worked on ten, each gets 0.10."* That is a task-COUNT weighting wearing person-time clothing — it does not weight by hours spent. A five-minute task and a four-day task carry identical weight for the same person. If AI-led tasks are systematically the small, numerous ones (plausible: defect diagnosis, sandbox policy, postmortems are the named leaf examples), the index reads high relative to an hours-weighted measure. MY OBSERVATION, NOT ANTHROPIC'S — flagged as the first thing to ask about when the next version publishes.**

Method, for the record: 20% of staff randomly sampled per week from **each department *"that make up the model R&D loop"*** (⚠️ **not company-wide**) through July 2026 → a Claude research agent read each sampled person's week (Slack + internal docs) → **~15,000 granular model R&D tasks** → organised into a tree of **542 nodes, 378 of them leaves** → agents gathered evidence, an independent Claude judge assigned the AL. **Crucially, each month is rated only on evidence from that month or earlier** (*"we only allow the research agents that do the ratings to see evidence from that month or earlier"*) — **so this is a genuine time series, not a back-cast of today's Claude onto old work.**

### 🔴🔴🔴 (4) THE AGENT POPULATION — THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL NUMBER IN THE DOCUMENT FOR THIS WIKI

> *"As of August 2026, there were approximately **30,000 agents** doing research and engineering work at Anthropic at any one time in our most-used internal platform. **These measurements cover this platform only.**"*

And the oversight stack around them: **100% of actions pass through an online monitor before execution**; *"We analyzed **over a billion decisions** from our research & engineering agents over August 2026 and found that **0.002% of them (about 1 in 47,000) were blocked**."* Offline, a classifier *"flags roughly 100,000 transcripts per week"*, of which *"the highest priority flags (**approximately ~50 per week**) are escalated to human review."*

🔴 **WHAT FALLS OUT OF THE TWO FIRST-PARTY FIGURES ALONE (no external chaining — both inputs HARD, from the same document):**

| Derived from the disclosed figures — ⚠️ **ALL ARE FLOORS AT ONE SIGNIFICANT FIGURE** (*"over a billion"* is a floor; *"approximately 30,000"* is 1sf) | |
|---|--:|
| Monitored decisions per **concurrent agent-slot**, August | **~33,000** (≥) |
| Per agent-slot per day | **~1,000** (≥) |
| Aggregate | **~370 decisions/sec** (≥) |
| One decision per agent-slot every… | **~80s** or faster |
| Blocked actions in August (0.002% at 1sf ⇒ 0.0015–0.0025%) | **~15,000–25,000** |
| Blocked actions flowing to human review | **~3,400–5,600/week** (*"humans review any blocked actions within one week"*) |

⚠️⚠️ **FOUR BASIS WARNINGS, ALL LOAD-BEARING — THIS TABLE IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS:**
1. **"~30,000 at any one time" is a CONCURRENCY STOCK, not a headcount.** Dividing a month's flow by it yields decisions per **concurrent agent-slot**, not per agent. If the agent population turns over within August there are more distinct agents than 30,000 and the per-agent figure is lower. The *intensity* readings (≈370/sec, one per ≈80s per slot) survive the relabelling; a "per agent" reading does not.
2. **Scope: *"These measurements cover this platform only."*** 30,000 is one internal platform's concurrent count — **not Anthropic's agent population.**
3. **The source says *"decisions"* but defines coverage over *"actions"*, and never equates the two.** Treating 1 decision = 1 action is ESTIMATE-grade, and every "action" reading above inherits it.
4. **NO DUTY-CYCLE VARIANT IS PUBLISHED.** An earlier draft of this block carried a "~27s at one-third duty" figure; it is **withdrawn** — the source already defines the population as agents *"doing research and engineering work… at any one time"*, i.e. active, so an idleness discount double-counts.

⛔ **WITHDRAWN AND RECORDED, BECAUSE IT WAS THE SAME FALLACY THIS ENTRY REJECTS ELSEWHERE:** an earlier draft cited the source's *"0.002%"* and *"about 1 in 47,000"* as two statements agreeing within 6% — presented as a source-quality check. **They are not two statements.** 1/47,000 = 0.0021277%, which rounds to 0.002% at one significant figure: **one measurement printed at two precisions, carrying zero corroborative information.** The claim is removed; the band above replaces it.

⛔ **WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID *NOT* DERIVE, AND WHY — because the obvious cross-multiplication is circular.** [[themes/tokenmaxxing]] carries an **explicitly un-adopted** OpenAI-side figure implying **~41 tokens/sec per agent** (130bn tokens ÷ 88h ÷ 10,000 agents, host-asserted). Chaining it here gives 30,000 × 41 = 1.23M tok/s ≈ **3.3 trillion tokens in August**, implying ~3,294 tokens per decision. **It looks like it corroborates — and it does not.** Applying Anthropic's own decision rate to the OpenAI run instead yields **3,297 tokens/decision**: the same number, because it is one equation rearranged, not an independent check. **One equation, two unknowns (tokens-per-decision and relative duty cycle); neither is identified.** Add that the 41 tok/s comes from a **burst** run of 10,000 agents at full tilt on a single problem while 30,000 is a **standing population** doing ordinary work, and the bases do not match either. ➤ **No internal token-burn figure is entered on this page. The document does not disclose enough to bound one.**

### 🔴🔴 (5) COMPUTE ALLOCATION — THE FIRST SAFETY-SHARE NUMBER FROM ANY LAB, AND IT IS ONE WEEK LONG

Over **13–20 July 2026**: *"about **6%** of compute that went to AI R&D was allocated toward safety, and about **12%** of compute that went to **AI-driven** AI R&D was allocated toward safety."*

⚠️⚠️ **TWO DENOMINATOR TRAPS, BOTH FATAL IF MISQUOTED. (a) 6% IS NOT 6% OF ANTHROPIC'S COMPUTE.** The denominator is the AI-R&D bucket, and **the document never discloses what share of total compute that bucket is.** Anyone reading this as *"Anthropic spends 6% of its compute on safety"* has been misled. **(b) *"AI-driven AI R&D"* — the denominator of the 12% — is NEVER DEFINED anywhere in the document.** A 12% with an undefined denominator is not a usable figure; it is carried here only as a quote. ⚠️ **Also material and easily missed: *"these metrics do not account for safeguards classifiers, which are a separate, comparable amount of compute."*** ⚠️ And a wobble in the source itself: it says in one place that a dual-purpose token *"was not counted in these metrics"* and in another that such work *"was also counted as AI R&D"* — different mechanics (excluded vs put in the denominator). Both push the safety share toward being a floor, but they are **not one consistent rule** and should not be quoted as such. **Footnote 2 also refuses a fixed reading outright: compute is managed as *"a single, fungible pool… this is a snapshot of how capacity happened to be directed in one week, not a fixed allocation."*** Method: every workload sorted into safety vs AI R&D, with Claude classifying; of *"almost 10,000"* **research training and evaluation runs** (⚠️ *almost* 10,000, i.e. below — and these are training/eval runs, **not** "compute runs": agent inference was handled by a separate classifier variant) they sampled **~14%**, weighted toward the highest-compute runs *"so that the result reflects where the compute actually went."*

- 🔴 **The 6%-vs-12% gap is the interesting part and Anthropic does not dwell on it: the safety share DOUBLES when the denominator narrows to AI-driven AI R&D.** ⚠️ **Do not read that as "agents do proportionally more safety work" without care — it is a ratio of two differently-scoped denominators, and the document gives no decomposition.**
- ⚠️ **Anthropic's own stated limits, which are unusually candid and should travel with the number: *"Safety research tends to use less compute than frontier training runs by its nature"*; *"compute is an imperfect proxy for how much a company focuses on safety"*; *"these are deliberately conservative estimates"*; underlying labels are *"best-effort, not verified"* and *"set by automated rules or occasionally by users"*; and the *"measurement covers one week"* — explicitly too short for a trend.** ➤ **One week, self-classified, on a metric the publisher concedes is a poor proxy. Logged as a baseline to compare future versions against, NOT as a fact about how much Anthropic spends on safety.**

| 07-26 | JPM · Samik Chatterjee / Arti Vula / Jaiden Patel ("Software Weekend Edition: Navigating Token Costs Through Federated Routing, SLMs, and Open-Weight Models") | margem | mixed | 🔴 **The most complete published price table on Anthropic's line now on this page — and, more importantly, the first "all-in cost to complete the same task" comparison against the Chinese open-weight models, which is a very different number from sticker price.** **Sticker (per million input/output tokens, company websites as of 7/21/26): Fable 5 $10.00/$50.00 — top of the entire spectrum; Opus 4.8 ~$5.00/$25.00; OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol ~$5.00/$30.00 (≤272K input); SpaceXAI Grok 4.5 $2.00/$6.00 (≤500K).** Two dated items net-new: **Sonnet 5 is running introductory pricing of $2/$10 through 8/31/26, reverting to $3/$15 on 9/1/26** (which supersedes nothing — the Barclays 07-17 row already carries $3/$15 as the standing rate — but it does mean the *effective* price rises ~50% on Sep 1), and **Opus 5.0, released 7/24/26, is priced at $5/$25** (same as Opus 4.8; JPM excludes it from the table because third-party benchmarking was not yet published). **The all-in numbers are the actionable part: total dollar cost to run the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — Fable 5 $5,631; Opus 4.8 $3,753; Kimi-K3 $2,710; qwen3.7-plus $311; deepseek-v4-flash $74.** So on a same-benchmark basis Fable 5 costs **~2.1x Kimi-K3, ~18x qwen3.7-plus and ~76x deepseek-v4-flash** — a far wider gap than sticker pricing implies, because the models consume very different token volumes to reach the same result. **The offsetting finding, and it is the more strategically important one: using Epoch AI's ECI score, JPM compared the quarterly average of the top three open-weight vs top three closed-weight models over ~3 years and found that "contrary to the popular investor perception, the performance difference… has remained relatively stable over the last couple of years, rather than materially converging."** The gap is not closing — but it is being held at a persistent cost disadvantage, which JPM reads as "a material positive for software companies" planning to build on open weights. Also: Anthropic is named inside **Microsoft's Foundry Model Router** and **Intuit's GenOS** as one of the models being routed *away from* for simple tasks — the mechanism by which enterprise token spend gets down-tiered. |
| 07-26 | R&Co Redburn · Alex Haissl ("Margin Call" roadshow feedback, via "Redburn 5") | margem | **bull** | **The sharpest published rebuttal to the row above, and it comes from a house that is bearish almost everything else in AI — with a first-person measurement from Claude Code itself.** Haissl's argument: "**This is about cost-per-task, not the sticker price of tokens.** The big pushback is that Chinese open-weight models (e.g. Kimi K3, GLM-5.2) now rival the closed frontier at a fraction of the headline price, which should crush token economics. **We think that overstates the real gap: Modern agentic workloads are dominated by cached tokens** — reused context (system prompt, conversation history) that is read from memory rather than recomputed via token spend. **In Alex's own Claude Code usage, he found stored-cache reads were ~98% of tokens, with fresh input under 2%.** Those open-weight models also **repeat failed tasks such as trying to go to a blocked website multiple times, while frontier models don't**. So while open-weight models look far cheaper on headline sticker pricing, **they're only 2x cheaper when you adjust for cache**." Put against the JPM table: **JPM's own all-in Fable-5-vs-Kimi-K3 ratio is ~2.1x, which is remarkably close to Redburn's cache-adjusted "2x"** — so the two houses may actually agree on the frontier-vs-Kimi gap, and the genuine dispute is over the cheap tail (qwen at ~18x, deepseek-v4-flash at ~76x on a headline-benchmark basis). That distinction is worth holding: **Anthropic's competitive exposure is not to Kimi-class models, which are within ~2x, but to the very cheap tier absorbing high-volume simple tasks** — which is exactly what the federated-routing architectures in the JPM row are built to do. |

**Quarter synthesis:** the debate is no longer "does Anthropic have real revenue?" (resolved: ~$47B run-rate, 70% GM, FCF+, overtook OpenAI on ARR and enterprise share). The 06-27 flow adds new angles across every dimension: (1) **$3T valuation framing** (Gavin Baker / All-In) — most concrete public buy-side price anchor to date; (2) **Claude Tag in Slack** — native distribution unlock embeds Anthropic in daily enterprise workflows beyond API; (3) **SpaceX TN+MS compute** — non-hyperscaler infrastructure eases the chronic intraday capacity squeeze; (4) **MSFT commercial alignment** — Azure Foundry now actively selling Anthropic, converting cloud commitment into distribution; (5) **GPT-5.6 Sol outperforms Mythos on Terminal-Bench 2.1** — first post-Fable benchmark reversal, though Mythos is export-restricted and return imminent (MS TMT 06-25); (6) **customer cost cuts 90%+** — usage deepens but ASP compresses as enterprises optimize; (7) **DeepSeek $7.4B** — China mobilizing at scale confirms the frontier gap is real. **06-29: White House partially lifts Mythos export controls** — a regulatory win that validates Anthropic's DC strategy and widens the government/international TAM; timing syncs with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 government rollout, accelerating the govt AI anchor-contract race. FundaAI's "fragile window" framing (GLM 5.2 ≈ Opus 4.6) is the key bear input: the frontier gap narrows over 12–18 months. The Gurley/@Hesamation bear camp (regulatory lobbying as competitive retreat signal) is now partially offset by the export-control win. **06-30:** two distribution/leverage positives — Rothschild flags Anthropic **renegotiating the Amazon deal in its own favor** ("flexing pricing power over Amazon," effective next year, now detailed as a shift from compute-hours to token-based billing that raises Amazon's costs and is prompting some Amazon engineers to distill Anthropic models pre-emptively), and The Information reports a **Claude agent coming to Microsoft Teams** (after the Salesforce/Slack tie-up), embedding Claude in both dominant enterprise collaboration surfaces as incumbents open their apps as agent app-stores. Offsetting: Rothschild also flags **Meta restricting Claude Code use** over distillation concerns (in place since May) — the same defensive dynamic now visible at two megacap counterparties — and JPMorgan (Wei Zheng Chan) reports the **$1.25bn/mo xAI Colossus 1 sale to Anthropic** alongside a flag that Anthropic's **ARR ceiling is reportedly compute-constrained**, sharpening the "chronically short on compute" bear case into an explicit revenue-ceiling risk. **07-01: the export-control thesis flips from "partial lift" to full lift** — The Information AM reports the White House has lifted Fable 5 export restrictions outright (superseding the 06-29 "partially lifts" framing — see Changelog), and Jefferies (Favuzza) confirms the operational follow-through: Fable 5 was redeployed overnight with tighter cybersecurity-task classifiers, with routine coding falling back to Opus 4.8 near-term. JPM's Data Center Watch desk adds a usage-durability data point — Opus 4.7 the only model top-5 in both volume and spend on OpenRouter in June — while Eurasia Group flags a political-economy risk (Anthropic-backed state-regulation PACs vs OpenAI-backed federal-preemption PACs, >$300mn projected 2026 election spend) and a scale claim (Fable/Mythos ~10T parameters). Bear counterpoint: The Information AM also reports Anthropic "backtracked" on spyware targeting Chinese users after controversy, and Vital Knowledge notes xAI's compute-resale customer list (Google + Anthropic) now parallels Meta's own new "Meta Compute" external-cloud pivot — i.e. Anthropic is simultaneously a compute buyer under ceiling pressure and one of several AI labs now normalizing compute resale as a category. **07-06 (MS TMT / Bernstein TMT / The Information / FT):** six datapoints span capital, distribution, competition and policy. Capital/supply: a fresh **WULF/WYKF 400MW Kentucky 20-year lease (~$19-20B, first power 2H'27, ~22% implied yield / ~85% NOI margin)** — a major frontier-training capacity add outside the AWS/Google/Azure/SpaceX stack (WULF +16-20%), directly relevant to the compute-ceiling bear case. Competition/margin (two-sided): The Information reports **AMZN is now evaluating OpenAI/Nova alternatives** to cut Claude dependence after the token-billing renegotiation raised its costs — confirming Anthropic's pricing leverage but sharpening the counterparty-substitution risk already visible at Meta; against that, a report that **small firms are replacing Salesforce with Claude** is the first SaaS-displacement (CRM) read-through, an application-layer TAM expansion. Distribution: **Claude agent for Microsoft Teams** re-confirmed (after the Salesforce/Slack tie-up). Policy: Anthropic is **tightening enforcement against Chinese access** (overseas entities/VPNs/"transfer stations"), and — a governance contrast relevant to the Gurley/@Hesamation lobbying debate — has **not** discussed a US-government stake, unlike OpenAI (reportedly a 5% stake). **07-07/08:** JPM's SpaceX deep-dive puts hard $/W math on the Colossus 1 rental (100% to Anthropic, $1.25bn/mo, ~$29/W blended) and sizes the Anthropic–Amazon Project Rainier New Carlisle facility at ~910MW (#2 operating AI facility globally). The capstone is SemiAnalysis's **07-08 IPO financials sneak-peek**: the ARR narrative re-accelerates past the spring $40-47B print to **>$60B (3Q26)** with the first hard profit mark — **3Q26 GAAP EBIT ~$1B (6% margin)** — and the clearest business-model contrast yet vs OpenAI (**API 75-85% of rev / subs just 15% of ARR / Consumer only ~5%** vs OpenAI ~40% consumer, ~−100% EBIT margin). The unit economics underwrite the compute arms-race the rest of the page tracks (Opus 4.8 API-token GM 80%+, ARR/MW ~$60M vs ~$16M 9 months ago, NNARR $10B+/mo, NRR ~500%), and SemiAnalysis's **$6T base-case valuation** (20x a modeled 2027 ending-ARR of $300B) is now the most aggressive public anchor on the page — above the 06-27 All-In/Gavin-Baker $3T framing. The debate has fully inverted: not "is the revenue real / is it profitable?" (resolved) but "can compute keep pace (>100GW combined w/ OpenAI by 2030) and does the frontier premium hold vs Chinese distillation + hyperscaler-lab catch-up." **07-10:** two fresh datapoints (both via @jukan05) reinforce both halves of the resolved debate. On profitability, **Dylan Patel's latest podcast confirms Anthropic turned free-cash-flow positive in Q2 and entered profitability — April and May both profitable and cash-flow positive, June trending the same** — upgrading the page's prior "adjusted-OI-positive-from-2Q26 / GAAP-EBIT-+$1B-in-3Q26" framing to an explicit *cash-flow*-positive print, at ARR >$50B / GM >70%. On the ARR curve, **Yipit's independent panel now marks ARR at $69B** (above SemiAnalysis's >$60B) with **daily net-adds accelerating from ~$400M to ~$550M/day vs May** — i.e. the curve is still steepening, and the highest independent ARR mark on the page is now Yipit's $69B. Two supply/capital reads round out the batch: Broadcom's Hock Tan (07-07) confirmed the **$35B XPV racks-leased-to-Anthropic (5-yr) mechanics** and that Anthropic **rents Google TPUs**, but **declined to comment on a future Anthropic ASIC program** (leaving the own-silicon question — which The Information 07-02 answered affirmatively — unconfirmed from the supplier side); and Bernstein (07-09) characterized the **Micron–Anthropic deal as vendor financing (supply guarantee for an equity stake)** rather than a cash prepay, a structure it argues doesn't de-risk Micron's investors — a nuance on the memory-lockup deals that themselves imply Anthropic's in-house accelerator. **07-10 (cont.) / 07-11:** Morgan Stanley's NVDA NDR with Jensen adds a silicon-mix read — **NVIDIA's share of Anthropic's compute has risen from negligible to ~50%** (Anthropic historically ASIC/Trainium-heavy; AI labs ~20% of total NVDA demand) — nuancing the "fungible multi-silicon" framing toward more NVDA content. "**Copilot Cowork enables Microsoft to leverage Anthropic's Claude Cowork harness natively inside Copilot**" (GA mid-June 2026), and UBS's judgment is that partnering with Anthropic "was **the best outcome for Microsoft given the pace of innovation at the model providers**" — while acknowledging that a sizeable share of investors read it as Microsoft conceding it was behind and "**forcing Microsoft to share the rents of Cowork**." That phrase is the Anthropic economics, embedded in the largest productivity install base in the world, and it is the strongest distribution datapoint on this page. **But the same checks show Microsoft privileging its own wrapper: Anthropic's Cowork "can integrate into OneDrive to view documents but it can't create… but Copilot Cowork can create a document"** — partner-and-gatekeeper, the concrete version of the Teams app-store dynamic already logged. Demand signals are engine-positive and meter-negative: "the excitement is that you can use **Claude as the backend engine**," against "**the consumption piece is a non-starter**" and a priced example ("6,500 credits, or **$65**" for one multi-source research task), with no head-to-head yet available — "we haven't seen the cost analysis of **Copilot Cowork vs Claude Cowork/ChatGPT**." Customer 4 states the decision rule the head-to-head will turn on: "if one's crazy more expensive than the other and they're technologically close, then **the commercial side will win**." Finally, the structural item: UBS frames the consensus investor view that a market "dominated by three frontier lab giants (**Anthropic**, OpenAI and Google) creates risk for the hyperscalers, with too much economic power concentrated in too few customers," and reads Satya's Jun/Jul blog campaign as Microsoft positioning explicitly against "the growing control/power of a few frontier AI model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI and Google)" — i.e. Anthropic's newest and largest distribution partner is publicly campaigning to commoditize Anthropic's layer, which is the distribution-vs-disintermediation tension on this page stated by a third party. **08-05 (FUNDA "Deep\|LLM: RSI…"):** the quarter's last input reframes the whole ARR debate rather than adding to it. FUNDA's argument is that the market is grading Anthropic on an application-layer question ("what is the next coding?") while the labs are running a capability roadmap (continual learning → self-evolution → full RSI), and the datapoints it brings are internal rather than commercial: **AI's contribution to Anthropic's own R&D velocity at 15–20% vs 5% six months earlier (Amodei, Feb-2026), company-wide AI-written code at 70–90% (~100% for frontline engineers; Boris Cherny at 22–27 PRs/day, none hand-written), "Claude Code builds Claude," Amodei's "possibly only 6–12 months away" Davos line, and METR's Jan-2026 mark of Claude Opus 4.5 at a 320-minute task horizon.** Read against the rest of this page, that is the mechanism underneath the coding-flywheel and out-invest-OpenAI theses already here — coding revenue funds compute, coding capability automates the lab's own R&D, and the compounding shows up first in cadence and cost curves rather than in a new vertical. Commercially it adds two things: **API revenue share 70–75% with eight-figure accounts DOUBLING IN SIX MONTHS** (the concrete evidence for the seat→usage→outcome pricing migration this page has been asserting), and **Claude for Excel live at Citi, RBC and Visa** plus **FDE hiring at scale** — the deployment mechanism that is supposed to compress the enterprise-adoption objection. **On the number that will get quoted: FUNDA's "run-rate reported above $70B by late July" is aggregated secondary reporting, is later than SemiAnalysis's >$60B (3Q26), and has been logged as a drift with the $60B mark kept in the series — it is directionally a third counterweight to the unverified 07-24 deceleration read, not a resolution of it.** Separately, a **2025-10-28 FUNDA AWS preview was backfilled as dated historical context** (no intra-quarter row — it predates the window): as of Oct-2025 only **Haiku 3.5 had successfully completed training on TRN2** (opus 3.5 and sonnet 3.5 both failed), Anthropic's **inference "remain[ed] predominantly on TPU"**, Project Rainier was planned to use **600k TRN2 chips to train "Claude 4+"**, and — the mechanism that scored best — Anthropic **"originally wrote in jax, which is more TPU-compatible, so when urgently needing compute they'll definitely prioritize TPU."** That is the origin of the TPU-vs-Trainium mix debate the page still tracks today. **RE-EVALUATED 2026-08-12 (/run-inbox, hyperscaler cluster — 4 back-dated sources, 07-28 → 08-12, three of them read-through from hyperscaler coverage and one a FIRST-PARTY expert call). The window's most valuable addition is not another ARR mark; it is the first credible view of WHAT ANTHROPIC PAYS AND WHY. ① THE SUPPLIER'S P&L IS NOW VISIBLE: GS (08-12) puts [[AMZN]]'s Project Rainier training workloads at ~15% EBITDA margin against ~40-45% for ordinary AWS workloads, and says the concessions are deliberate and durable — "they're willing to dilute their margins… because they think the inference opportunity over the long term is very, very strong," and would be "surprised" to see AWS reprice them. ➜ Anthropic is capturing most of the surplus on the training leg, and the reported AWS margin is being carried by everything except Anthropic. Anthropic is at the BOTTOM of the current range, not the top. ③ THE STRATEGIC DIRECTION GOT A NUMBER AND A DATE FROM THE INSIDE: an Anthropic infrastructure practitioner (07-28) expects ~30% own data centres / 60% hyperscalers / 10% neoclouds within three years, because "the end goal is TO NOT BE DOWNSTREAM… they want to be completely vertically integrated, LIKE HOW [[GOOG]] IS." Alongside it sits the first hard training-run figure this page has carried: Mythos pre-training at “SUB-200 MEGAWATTS” for about two months against a multi-gigawatt fleet — the coordination ceiling stated as a fact, and the best evidence available that fleet size and frontier capability are only loosely coupled today.** **One item is left deliberately OPEN and has been given its own Signal-vs-management row: SemiAnalysis’s written 27%-of-net-new-GW figure and Patel’s ~30%-rising-to-40-50% figure are the same house four days apart, plausibly measuring different objects. Four per-GW bases now circulate (Anthropic ARR $30bn · fully-loaded cost ~$5bn/yr · AVGO content $11-15bn · hardware infra $20-30bn) plus the separate $16M/MW/yr contract-revenue mark. Never netted.**

**➜ 2026-09-06 UPDATE (/wiki-ingest — 4 sources: The Information · Valida Pau, "How Anthropic Clinched $517 Billion in Compute Deals in 11 Months", 2026-09-06 ⚠️ *PAYWALLED — opening only, body UNREAD*; The Information, "Anthropic’s IPO plans, Cognition’s $900M revenue pace…", 2026-09-06; Susquehanna · Mehdi Hosseini, "Technology Hardware — August 30–September 5 Weekly Summary, Outlook", 2026-09-05 ⚠️ *headline-only relays, articles unread*; @aleabitoreddit, corpus, 2026-09-06 ⚠️ *not a broker*. **NOTHING ON THIS PAGE IS SUPERSEDED — every figure, deal size, valuation mark and Signal stands; all four items are additive.**) **THE SYNTHESIS IN ONE LINE: the question the 09-04/09-05 flow said IPO investors were pressing — revenue per gigawatt — now has HALF an answer, and it is the OUTSIDE-IN half.** A journalist’s triangulation puts Anthropic at **~15.8-16.8GW of contracted capacity against $517bn of compute deals in 11 months**, i.e. **~$31-33bn per GW of BUYER-SIDE, MULTI-YEAR PURCHASE COMMITMENT** — a FIFTH per-GW basis that must never be netted against the ~$16M/MW/yr contract revenue, the [[NVDA]] revenue-per-GW ladder, the ~$30-60bn/GW build cost, [[TSM]]’s 30-40GW/yr built, or the four [[AVGO]]-call bases. **It is NOT adopted as a ratio**: the numerator is an outside estimate under the outlet’s own *"never publicly disclosed"* caveat, the term is undefined so no per-year figure exists, and the denominator is capacity *"it could tap"* — an option ceiling. What it DOES do is (a) corroborate the capacity ladder from a third independent direction, pushing the page’s standing *"~10+ GW"* to the low end, and (b) expose the real hole: **only $80bn of the $517bn (Lambda $35bn + Nscale $45bn, both already logged and NOT re-counted) is attached to a named, sized counterparty — ~85% is not.** The IPO side moved in the same window but did not resolve: the secondary-plus-long-lockup structure got a second dated sourcing, while a **$2T / "next month"** valuation appeared from an X account with no source shown — **NOT ADOPTED**, kept alongside the three other $2T references, against the only PRICED mark of **$965bn post (Series H, May-2026)**, a ~2.1x gap. ➤ **THE FALSIFIABLE TEST IS UNCHANGED AND NOW SHARPER: does the S-1 carry EITHER a total-contracted-compute line OR a compute-cost / purchase-commitment line? That binary converts ~$31-33bn/GW from arithmetic into economics, and it is the same binary the 09-05 run flagged as the highest-value disclosure watch on this wiki.**

Corroborating demand-side behaviour, WSJ (07-26): **"CTOs… utilizing lower-cost, open-source models from China for most tasks and reserving only the most specialized and complex queries for OpenAI and Anthropic"** — down-tiering as observed behaviour, which is compatible with revenue growth *if* the retained queries are the valuable ones. That remains the unresolved question and it is the same one behind the 07-22 UBS and 07-24 Rothschild/TickerTrends bear datapoints. **Fifth, capability evidence: a live Claude Code demo built a portfolio-monitoring dashboard in 10 minutes at BofA's Transforming World Conference**, alongside the (methodology-free, so treat loosely) claim that **AI has cut the cost of a due-diligence report by 99.98% in three years**.
